nodes.title: MONA: Myopic Optimization with Non-myopic Approval Can Mitigate Multi-step Reward Hacking
nodes.abstract: Future advanced AI systems may learn sophisticated strategies through reinforcement learning (RL) that humans cannot understand well enough to safely evaluate. We propose a training method which avoids agents learning undesired multi-step plans that receive high reward (multi-step "reward hacks") even if humans are not able to detect that the behaviour is undesired. The method, Myopic Optimization with Non-myopic App...
nodes.delta: [Evolution • Self] We study MONA empirically in three settings which model different misalignment failure modes including 2-step environments with LLMs representing delegated oversight and encoded reasoning and longer-horizon gridworld environments representing sensor tampering.

nodes.title: Paper Quality Assessment based on Individual Wisdom Metrics from Open Peer Review
authors: Jasper J. F. van den Bosch
nodes.abstract: Traditional closed peer review systems, which have played a central role in scientific publishing, are often slow, costly, non-transparent, stochastic, and possibly subject to biases - factors that can impede scientific progress and undermine public trust. Here, we propose and examine the efficacy and accuracy of an alternative form of scientific peer review: through an open, bottom-up process. First, using data from...
nodes.delta: [Safety • Memory] First, using data from two major scientific conferences (CCN2023 and ICLR2023), we highlight how high variability of review scores and low correlation across reviewers presents a challenge for collective review.

nodes.title: Provably-Safe Neural Network Training Using Hybrid Zonotope Reachability Analysis
nodes.abstract: Even though neural networks are being increasingly deployed in safety-critical control applications, it remains difficult to enforce constraints on their output, meaning that it is hard to guarantee safety in such settings. While many existing methods seek to verify a neural network's satisfaction of safety constraints, few address how to correct an unsafe network. The handful of works that extract a training signal ...
nodes.delta: [Manipulation • Action] We demonstrate the practicality of our method by training a forward-invariant neural network controller for an affine dynamical system with a non-convex input set, as well as generating safe reach-avoid plans for a black-box dynamical system.

nodes.title: Data Science Students Perspectives on Learning Analytics: An Application of Human-Led and LLM Content Analysis
nodes.abstract: Objective This study is part of a series of initiatives at a UK university designed to cultivate a deep understanding of students' perspectives on analytics that resonate with their unique learning needs. It explores collaborative data processing undertaken by postgraduate students who examined an Open University Learning Analytics Dataset (OULAD). Methods A qualitative approach was adopted, integrating a Retrieval-A...
nodes.delta: [Safety • Memory] While human-led content analysis provided a general understanding of students' perspectives, the LLM offered nuanced insights.

nodes.title: Optimizing Return Distributions with Distributional Dynamic Programming
nodes.abstract: We introduce distributional dynamic programming (DP) methods for optimizing statistical functionals of the return distribution, with standard reinforcement learning as a special case. Previous distributional DP methods could optimize the same class of expected utilities as classic DP. To go beyond, we combine distributional DP with stock augmentation, a technique previously introduced for classic DP in the context of...
nodes.delta: [Reinforcement • Reward] To highlight the practical potential of stock-augmented return distribution optimization and distributional DP, we introduce an agent that combines DQN and the core ideas of distributional DP, and empirically evaluate it for solving instances of the applications discussed.

nodes.title: GPUs, CPUs, and... NICs: Rethinking the Network's Role in Serving Complex AI Pipelines
nodes.abstract: The increasing prominence of AI necessitates the deployment of inference platforms for efficient and effective management of AI pipelines and compute resources. As these pipelines grow in complexity, the demand for distributed serving rises and introduces much-dreaded network delays. In this paper, we investigate how the network can instead be a boon to the excessively high resource overheads of AI pipelines. To alle...
nodes.delta: [Manipulation • Action] We explore the challenges and opportunities of offloading, and propose a research agenda for integrating network hardware into AI pipelines, unlocking new opportunities for optimization.

nodes.title: AdaWM: Adaptive World Model based Planning for Autonomous Driving
nodes.abstract: World model based reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a promising approach for autonomous driving, which learns a latent dynamics model and uses it to train a planning policy. To speed up the learning process, the pretrain-finetune paradigm is often used, where online RL is initialized by a pretrained model and a policy learned offline. However, naively performing such initialization in RL may result in dramat...
nodes.delta: [Manipulation • Action] Extensive experiments on the challenging CARLA driving tasks demonstrate that AdaWM significantly improves the finetuning process, resulting in more robust and efficient performance in autonomous driving systems.

nodes.title: Autonomy-of-Experts Models
nodes.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models mostly use a router to assign tokens to specific expert modules, activating only partial parameters and often outperforming dense models. We argue that the separation between the router's decision-making and the experts' execution is a critical yet overlooked issue, leading to suboptimal expert selection and ineffective learning. To address this, we propose Autonomy-of-Experts (AoE), a...
nodes.delta: [Graph • Diffusion] We pre-train language models having 700M up to 4B parameters, demonstrating that AoE outperforms traditional MoE models with comparable efficiency.

nodes.title: Evolution and The Knightian Blindspot of Machine Learning
nodes.abstract: This paper claims that machine learning (ML) largely overlooks an important facet of general intelligence: robustness to a qualitatively unknown future in an open world. Such robustness relates to Knightian uncertainty (KU) in economics, i.e. uncertainty that cannot be quantified, which is excluded from consideration in ML's key formalisms. This paper aims to identify this blind spot, argue its importance, and cataly...
nodes.delta: [Code • Skill] Interestingly, evolution achieves such robustness without explicit theory, formalisms, or mathematical gradients.

nodes.title: Boosting MCTS with Free Energy Minimization
nodes.abstract: Active Inference, grounded in the Free Energy Principle, provides a powerful lens for understanding how agents balance exploration and goal-directed behavior in uncertain environments. Here, we propose a new planning framework, that integrates Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) with active inference objectives to systematically reduce epistemic uncertainty while pursuing extrinsic rewards. Our key insight is that MCTS al...
nodes.delta: [Reinforcement • Reward] Empirically, we benchmark our planner on a diverse set of continuous control tasks, where it demonstrates performance gains over both standalone CEM and MCTS with random rollouts.

nodes.title: Belief-Contraction-Driven Active Inverse Source Localization and Characterization
nodes.abstract: Active inverse source localization and characterization (ISLC) in dynamic fields requires sequential decision making under partial observability, where a mobile sensor must infer latent source parameters from sparse, noisy readings. We introduce a belief-contraction-driven approach that unifies inference, stopping, and control. An attention-augmented particle filter stabilizes Bayesian belief updates through ESS-base...
nodes.delta: [World • Forecasting] Across seven field modalities, spatial out-of-distribution tests, and nonstationary source shifts, our agent (ATT-PFRL) achieves higher completion, faster convergence, and more accurate localization than planning and RL+Bayes baselines under similar computation.

nodes.title: Infinite Time Turing Machines and their Applications
nodes.abstract: This work establishes a rigorous theoretical foundation for analyzing deep learning systems by leveraging Infinite Time Turing Machines (ITTMs), which extend classical computation into transfinite ordinal steps. Using ITTMs, we reinterpret modern architectures like Transformers, revealing fundamental limitations in scalability, efficiency, and interpretability. Building on these insights, we propose the Universal Sta...
nodes.delta: [Evolution • Self] Building on these insights, we propose the Universal State Machine (USM), a novel computational paradigm designed from first principles.

nodes.title: Guaranteed Recovery of Unambiguous Clusters
nodes.abstract: Clustering is often a challenging problem because of the inherent ambiguity in what the "correct" clustering should be. Even when the number of clusters [MATH] is known, this ambiguity often still exists, particularly when there is variation in density among different clusters, and clusters have multiple relatively separated regions of high density. In this paper we propose an information-theoretic characterization o...
nodes.delta: [Image • Visual] In this paper we propose an information-theoretic characterization of when a [MATH]-clustering is ambiguous, and design an algorithm that recovers the clustering whenever it is unambiguous.

nodes.title: Robust Representation Consistency Model via Contrastive Denoising
nodes.abstract: Robustness is essential for deep neural networks, especially in security-sensitive applications. To this end, randomized smoothing provides theoretical guarantees for certifying robustness against adversarial perturbations. Recently, diffusion models have been successfully employed for randomized smoothing to purify noise-perturbed samples before making predictions with a standard classifier. While these methods exce...
nodes.delta: [Graph • Diffusion] For example, our method outperforms the certified accuracy of diffusion-based methods on ImageNet across all perturbation radii by 5.3% on average, with up to 11.6% at larger radii, while reducing inference costs by 85[MATH] on average.

nodes.title: Foundation Models for CPS-IoT: Opportunities and Challenges
nodes.abstract: Methods from machine learning (ML) have transformed the implementation of Perception-Cognition-Communication-Action loops in Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) and the Internet of Things (IoT), replacing mechanistic and basic statistical models with those derived from data. However, the first generation of ML approaches, which depend on supervised learning with annotated data to create task-specific models, faces significa...
nodes.delta: [Reinforcement • Reward] We also propose actions by CPS-IoT researchers to collaborate in developing key community resources necessary for establishing FMs and LLMs as foundational tools for the next generation of CPS-IoT systems.

nodes.title: Blockchain-based Crowdsourced Deep Reinforcement Learning as a Service
nodes.abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for solving complex problems. However, its full potential remains inaccessible to a broader audience due to its complexity, which requires expertise in training and designing DRL solutions, high computational capabilities, and sometimes access to pre-trained models. This necessitates the need for hassle-free services that increase the availability o...
nodes.delta: [Evolution • Self] To enhance the accessibility to DRL services, this paper proposes a novel blockchain-based crowdsourced DRL as a Service (DRLaaS) framework.

nodes.title: UAV-assisted Internet of Vehicles: A Framework Empowered by Reinforcement Learning and Blockchain
nodes.abstract: This paper addresses the challenges of selecting relay nodes and coordinating among them in UAV-assisted Internet-of-Vehicles (IoV). The selection of UAV relay nodes in IoV employs mechanisms executed either at centralized servers or decentralized nodes, which have two main limitations: 1) the traceability of the selection mechanism execution and 2) the coordination among the selected UAVs, which is currently offered...
nodes.delta: [Reinforcement • Reward] The evaluation results demonstrate that the proposed selection and coordination mechanisms improve the stability of the selected relays and maximize the coverage and connectivity achieved by the UAVs.

nodes.title: QuFeX: Quantum feature extraction module for hybrid quantum-classical deep neural networks
nodes.abstract: We introduce Quantum Feature Extraction (QuFeX), a novel quantum machine learning module. The proposed module enables feature extraction in a reduced-dimensional space, significantly decreasing the number of parallel evaluations required in typical quantum convolutional neural network architectures. Its design allows seamless integration into deep classical neural networks, making it particularly suitable for hybrid ...
nodes.delta: [Image • Visual] Our numerical analysis indicates that the Qu-Net can achieve superior segmentation performance compared to a U-Net baseline.

nodes.title: Learning in Log-Domain: Subthreshold Analog AI Accelerator Based on Stochastic Gradient Descent
nodes.abstract: The rapid proliferation of AI models, coupled with growing demand for edge deployment, necessitates the development of AI hardware that is both high-performance and energy-efficient. In this paper, we propose a novel analog accelerator architecture designed for AI/ML training workloads using stochastic gradient descent with L2 regularization (SGDr). The architecture leverages log-domain circuits in subthreshold MOS a...
nodes.delta: [World • Forecasting] Experimental results demonstrate that the architecture closely approximates ideal behavior, with a mean square error below 0.87% and precision as low as 8 bits.

nodes.title: A Spatio-temporal Graph Network Allowing Incomplete Trajectory Input for Pedestrian Trajectory Prediction
nodes.abstract: Pedestrian trajectory prediction is important in the research of mobile robot navigation in environments with pedestrians. Most pedestrian trajectory prediction algorithms require the input historical trajectories to be complete. If a pedestrian is unobservable in any frame in the past, then its historical trajectory become incomplete, the algorithm will not predict its future trajectory. To address this limitation, ...
nodes.delta: [World • Forecasting] Experiments on public datasets show that STGN-IT outperforms state of the art algorithms on these metrics.

nodes.title: Advanced Physics-Informed Neural Network with Residuals for Solving Complex Integral Equations
nodes.abstract: In this paper, we present the Residual Integral Solver Network (RISN), a novel neural network architecture designed to solve a wide range of integral and integro-differential equations, including one-dimensional, multi-dimensional, ordinary and partial integro-differential, systems, fractional types, and Helmholtz-type integral equations involving oscillatory kernels. RISN integrates residual connections with high-ac...
nodes.delta: [World • Forecasting] Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate that RISN consistently outperforms not only classical PINNs but also advanced variants such as Auxiliary PINN (A-PINN) and Self-Adaptive PINN (SA-PINN), achieving significantly lower Mean Absolute Errors (MAE) across various types of equations.

nodes.title: SRMT: Shared Memory for Multi-agent Lifelong Pathfinding
nodes.abstract: Coordination in decentralized multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) necessitates that agents share information about their behavior and intentions. Existing approaches rely on communication protocols with domain or resource constraints or centralized training that poorly scales to large agent populations. We introduce the Shared Recurrent Memory Transformer (SRMT), which enables coordination through unconstrained...
nodes.delta: [Reinforcement • Reward] These results demonstrate that a transformer with shared recurrent memory enhances coordination in decentralized multi-agent systems.

nodes.title: Optimizing the Optimizer for Physics-Informed Neural Networks and Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
nodes.abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have revolutionized the computation of PDE solutions by integrating partial differential equations (PDEs) into the neural network's training process as soft constraints, becoming an important component of the scientific machine learning (SciML) ecosystem. More recently, physics-informed Kolmogorv-Arnold networks (PIKANs) have also shown to be effective and comparable in accura...
nodes.delta: [World • Forecasting] Our findings provide state-of-the-art results with orders-of-magnitude accuracy improvements without the use of adaptive weights or any other enhancements typically employed in PINNs.

nodes.title: Let SSMs be ConvNets: State-space Modeling with Optimal Tensor Contractions
nodes.abstract: We introduce Centaurus, a class of networks composed of generalized state-space model (SSM) blocks, where the SSM operations can be treated as tensor contractions during training. The optimal order of tensor contractions can then be systematically determined for every SSM block to maximize training efficiency. This allows more flexibility in designing SSM blocks beyond the depthwise-separable configuration commonly i...
nodes.delta: [Graph • Diffusion] We show that this heterogeneous network design outperforms its homogeneous counterparts in raw audio processing tasks including keyword spotting, speech denoising, and automatic speech recognition (ASR).

nodes.title: Pretraining and Test-Time Training Budgets Matter for ARC: A Controlled Study of VARC and TRM
nodes.abstract: The Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC) is increasingly used to evaluate whether neural networks can infer task-specific transformations from few demonstrations. Recent ARC models differ in architecture, but also in broader training and evaluation protocols, including pretraining data, data augmentation, test-time setup, and optimization budgets, making conclusions about architecture benefits debatable. In this wo...
nodes.delta: ✨ [LLM Verified Delta] Prior comparative evaluations of ARC models conflated genuine architectural merits with disparate resource allocations due to inconsistent pretraining data, test-time training (TTT) setups, and optimization compute budgets. To isolate these effects, this paper introduces a standardized inductive evaluation protocol that systematically crosses five pretraining budgets with four TTT budgets by explicitly decoupling and controlling task-variant counts and total sample presentations across the VARC and TRM architectures.

nodes.title: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Automated Tuning of Specialized Neural Network Models
nodes.abstract: Many machine learning approaches are two-level: an expert selects a class of methods, within this class the choice of key components is critical and usually manual. This paper addresses the automatic tuning of these components and proposes a framework transferable across models of different nature. The multi-agent large language model (LLM) framework has three roles---analyst, coder, and recorder~---with an experimen...
nodes.delta: ✨ [LLM Verified Delta] Prior automated optimization frameworks are typically limited to either rigid, predefined discrete search spaces or unconstrained end-to-end script generation, which frequently compromises pipeline stability and fails to effectively tune complex, domain-specific internal mechanisms. To resolve this, the authors introduce a sandboxed, role-specialized multi-agent LLM framework (analyst, coder, and recorder) that operates over an open yet semantically targeted functional space, iteratively synthesizing code exclusively for designated sub-components while keeping the global model architecture invariant.

nodes.title: A Step Harder, Not a Step Too Far: The Benefits and Limits of Curriculum Difficulty Progression in GRPO
nodes.abstract: Curriculum learning typically organizes training samples from easy to hard. In GRPO, medium-difficulty samples are attractive for online selection because they are more likely to yield informative group-relative learning signals, and prioritizing them can improve training efficiency. However, it remains unclear whether persistently selecting such samples also leads to the strongest final model performance, or whether...
nodes.delta: ✨ [LLM Verified Delta] Prior online curriculum methods in GRPO rely on static difficulty metrics that rapidly desynchronize from the evolving policy and persistently restrict sample selection to medium-difficulty instances, limiting final task performance. To address this, the authors introduce dynamic on-policy difficulty re-estimation paired with a staged curriculum that progressively shifts the active sampling band toward moderately harder problems while explicitly bounding progression to prevent performance degradation from overly difficult regimes.

nodes.title: Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction
nodes.abstract: Large language models struggle to reliably identify and correct errors in their own reasoning. Unlike prior training-based approaches that fine-tune an LLM to generate revisions or feedback, we learn where to intervene in failed rollouts and determine how to redirect them. To choose where to intervene, we train a 130K-parameter MLP head on a frozen encoder using only final-answer correctness. For redirection, we find...
nodes.delta: ✨ [LLM Verified Delta] Prior self-correction methods either demand costly model fine-tuning to generate revisions or rely on inline reflection-token injections that fail to reliably alter reasoning trajectories and locate failure points without dense step-level supervision. To resolve this, UPTURN trains a lightweight MLP probe on frozen representations using solely outcome-level supervision to identify the optimal intervention point, then executes training-free redirection by truncating the reasoning trace and injecting a corrective instruction as a distinct user turn rather than an inline token.

nodes.title: Not All Dimensions Are Equal: Outlier-Aware Attention Linearization with Grouped Quadratic Kernels
nodes.abstract: Linearizing softmax attention offers a route to efficient Transformer inference, but preserving pretrained attention remains challenging. We identify an important source of approximation error overlooked by standard linearization methods: a small number of outlier dimensions contribute disproportionately to query-key dot products and account for a large fraction of the approximation error. Motivated by this heterogen...
nodes.delta: ✨ [LLM Verified Delta] Prior quadratic attention linearization methods, such as standard Taylor expansions and DiJiang, rely on globally uniform coefficients that treat all latent dimensions identically, failing to capture sparse outlier dimensions that disproportionately dominate query-key dot products and attention approximation error. To resolve this, OAL introduces a Hadamard-product-based quadratic kernel that enables dimension-specific interactions, grouping feature dimensions by contribution scale to isolate high-impact outliers with dedicated coefficients while maintaining strictly linear-time sequence evaluation.

nodes.title: Variance-Reduced Policy Gradient is Nearly Minimax-Optimal
nodes.abstract: Standard Policy Gradient (PG) algorithms suffer from high estimation variance because they rely on Monte Carlo updates. While off-policy variance reduction mitigates this problem, establishing optimal sample complexity currently requires either restrictive assumptions, such as uniformly bounded importance weights, or impractical second-order operations. In this work, we introduce Loopless Variance-Reduced PG (LVR-PG)...
nodes.delta: ✨ [LLM Verified Delta] Prior variance-reduced policy gradient algorithms could only achieve optimal sample complexity by relying on impractical second-order operations or imposing restrictive assumptions such as uniformly bounded importance weights. To overcome this, this work introduces Loopless Variance-Reduced Policy Gradient (LVR-PG), a unified first-order framework integrating recursive variance-reduced updates with defensive importance sampling to achieve a nearly minimax-optimal $\tilde{O}(\epsilon^{-3})$ last-iterate sample complexity under weak gradient domination.

nodes.title: Calibration in One Go: Jointly Learning Accurate and Calibrated Neural Networks
nodes.abstract: Neural networks (NNs), while highly flexible and versatile, are often poorly calibrated. Post-hoc calibration methods adjust the outputs of an already trained model using a separate calibration dataset and additional calibration parameters. This process adds overhead that requires separate optimization of the calibrator and subsequent model selection. In this paper, we show that standard (post-hoc) calibrators can be...
nodes.delta: [World • Forecasting] Our approach outperforms SOTA calibrators with minimal added complexity, while also avoiding the multiplicative overhead of separate calibration components in settings such as multi-task learning.

nodes.title: A Baseline Assessment for the Agentic Web Technology Stack
nodes.abstract: The fast pace in which protocols, frameworks, and technologies are being proposed for LLM-based agents results in a complex scenario for anyone aiming to create state-of-the-art AI solutions. Without an assessment on how different protocols, frameworks, and libraries work together to compose an Agentic Web solution, developers and organizations face different challenges (e.g., skilling, governance, infrastructure) ev...
nodes.delta: [Code • Skill] With the presented results, we expect to present a baseline in terms of metrics and results for this complex and fast evolving scenario for those aiming at designing, assessing, and developing multi-agent systems.

nodes.title: Adaptive DHiSparse: Speculative Decoding over a Load-Adaptive KV Hierarchy
nodes.abstract: Long-context serving runs out of KV memory before the hardware reaches its useful throughput. HiSparse stores history in host memory and fetches only the selected entries, but it uses one cache budget at every load and does not handle draft-model speculative decoding such as DSpark and DFlash2. We present Adaptive DHiSparse, which supports speculative decoding over hierarchical sparse KV and adapts residency to load....
nodes.delta: [Image • Visual] We present Adaptive DHiSparse, which supports speculative decoding over hierarchical sparse KV and adapts residency to load.

nodes.title: Amortized Counterfactual Prediction with Graph Neural Networks
nodes.abstract: Counterfactual inference asks how an observed outcome might have differed under different circumstances, such as whether a patient would have recovered had they received a different treatment. Such questions arise whenever decisions depend on the outcomes of alternatives that were not observed. Answering counterfactual queries generally requires knowledge of the underlying causal structure, which is often unavailable...
nodes.delta: [Graph • Diffusion] Across synthetic and image-based benchmarks, CFGNP achieves stronger predictive performance than existing approaches, including on the German Loan benchmark, where it reduces MSE from [MATH] to [MATH].

nodes.title: Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench 2.0: Automating Diverse Task Construction and Measuring Sustained Agent Progress
nodes.abstract: Long-horizon terminal benchmarks measure whether an agent can sustain progress through extended workflows with process rewards, not only whether its final state passes a binary check. We present Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench 2.0 (LHTB 2.0), an extension of Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench that preserves its 46 original tasks while correcting task and evaluation-infrastructure defects and extending 31 tasks. LHTB 2.0 contain...
nodes.delta: [Code • Skill] We present Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench 2.0 (LHTB 2.0), an extension of Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench that preserves its 46 original tasks while correcting task and evaluation-infrastructure defects and extending 31 tasks.

nodes.title: LAPT-Scale: Scaling Embodied Policies with Latent Action Pre-Training on Human Videos
nodes.abstract: Scaling generalist robotic policies is limited by the high cost of collecting embodied interaction data. Large-scale egocentric human videos offer a rich alternative, but they lack robot action labels, and existing action annotation methods are often noisy under real-world visual complexity and diverse manipulation dynamics. We introduce LAPT-Scale, a scalable latent action pre-training paradigm with two components: ...
nodes.delta: [Manipulation • Action] Unlike prior vector-quantized LAMs, LAPT-Scale-LAM uses a continuous latent space to preserve fine-grained motion and interaction dynamics.

nodes.title: Orthros: Phase-Aware Heterogeneous Attention for Efficient Transformers
nodes.abstract: Efficient attention mechanisms, such as linear and sliding window attention, aim to reduce the computational complexity of Transformers from quadratic to linear. However, their degraded in-context recall often necessitates interleaving full attention layers, leaving the quadratic bottleneck unresolved in long-context processing. To address this, we introduce Orthros attention, which shifts the efficiency paradigm fro...
nodes.delta: [Graph • Diffusion] Finally, Orthros achieves a [MATH] prefilling speedup over Transformers with end-to-end inference gains, while preserving long-context capabilities, as demonstrated by near-perfect 128K needle-in-a-haystack results and Transformer-level performance on real-world in-context recall tasks.

nodes.title: SafeDiSTL: Decomposing Joint Constraints for Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
nodes.abstract: Cooperative multi-agent tasks often impose constraints on a shared objective or collective safety. A team level violation cost function can measure this constraint outcome, but does not distinguish which agents' actions most strongly influence that violation. We present SafeDiSTL, a constrained multi-agent reinforcement learning framework that allows for credit assignment even with joint constraint measurements. We u...
nodes.delta: [Reinforcement • Reward] Results demonstrate a strong improvement of the learned policy in dealing with shared constraint while retaining the performance of unconstrained policies.

nodes.title: A Privileged Teacher That Only Scores Cannot Search: Critique-Conditioned On-Policy Self-Distillation for Reasoning
nodes.abstract: On-policy self-distillation promises to replace the sparse outcome signal of verifiable-reward RL with dense token-level credit: a teacher conditioned on the reference solution scores the student's own rollout, and the resulting distributional shift is distilled back into the policy. nodes.title: Matched-Context Group Policy Optimization for LLM Agent Training
nodes.abstract: Training long-horizon language model agents requires assigning credit to intermediate decisions from sparse terminal feedback. nodes.delta: [Evolution • Self] Three-seed factorial controls support opposite-fold evidence and evidence weighting; joint state-rubric matching achieves the highest mean in all four representation-control settings.

nodes.title: VETNET: Assembling Benchmark Datasets for AI-Driven Veterinary Innovation
nodes.abstract: VETNET represents an ecosystem of live benchmark datasets and evaluation frameworks designed to accelerate AI-driven innovation in animal science and veterinary medicine through standardized, high-quality datasets and multi-institutional collaboration across academic and non-academic sectors. This framework addresses the gap between AI advances in human medicine and the fragmented state of veterinary AI development.
nodes.delta: [Clinical • Medical] VETNET represents an ecosystem of live benchmark datasets and evaluation frameworks designed to accelerate AI-driven innovation in animal science and veterinary medicine through standardized, high-quality datasets and multi-institutional collaboration across academic and non-academic sectors.

nodes.title: Beyond Discrimination: Evaluating Probability Calibration in Radiomics-Image Fusion for Renal Cell Carcinoma Classification
nodes.abstract: Reliable probability estimates are important for the clinical interpretation of machine-learning classifiers, yet radiomics--image fusion models for renal cell carcinoma (RCC) are commonly evaluated primarily by discrimination. Using 396 patients from the KiTS23 dataset, we evaluated whether adding radiomics to four image-model families improved probabilistic performance in addition to discrimination. Seventeen indiv...

nodes.title: When Edge Independence Fails: Joint Graph Diffusion with Latent Sociability Priors
nodes.abstract: Discrete graph diffusion models corrupt graph structure through independent edge updates with a Markovian noise model. Combined with the exchangeability requirement on the output distribution, the terminal prior is necessarily an Erdős--Rényi (E-R) random graph. nodes.title: DualQuant: Dual-scale Calibration-free Weight-and-Activation Quantization for LLMs
nodes.abstract: Low-bit inference on accelerators with native 4-bit support requires quantizing both weights and activations to realize the full throughput gains these formats provide. While post-training weight quantization has been extensively studied, activation quantization remains considerably more challenging and typically requires calibration data. In this work, we introduce DUALQUANT, a dual-scale, calibration-free post-trai...
nodes.delta: [Image • Visual] Across Llama and Qwen models evaluated on WikiText-2, C4, and zero-shot downstream tasks, DUALQUANT matches or exceeds the accuracy of calibration-based SmoothQuant across most models and formats, and substantially outperforms calibration-free baselines, with large gains for MX and NV block formats.

nodes.title: Beyond Gate Weights: Decision-Level Interpretation of Radiomics-Image Feature Fusion for RCC Classification
nodes.abstract: Gate coefficients describe how a fusion layer weights intermediate features, but they do not necessarily reflect the magnitude of branch contributions at the classifier output. We investigate this distinction in a fixed 3D MedVAE--radiomics model for clear cell versus non-clear cell renal cell carcinoma classification from contrast-enhanced CT. Because the model uses a linear classification head, the binary decision ...
nodes.delta: [Clinical • Medical] These findings show that structural gate weighting and decision-level branch contribution represent distinct aspects of gated feature fusion and should be interpreted separately.

nodes.title: ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State
nodes.abstract: State-space models (SSMs) maintain a fixed-size recurrent state, but reading and writing it at every decoding step can bottleneck hybrid models. This eager state management causes large state I/O with low arithmetic intensity, leaves speculative decoding no cheap rollback, and feeds state quantization error into subsequent recurrent updates. nodes.title: UkrMeme: Multimodal Explainable Persuasion Detection in Ukrainian Memes
nodes.abstract: Memes play a central role in modern online communication, especially in contexts of political conflict where visual and textual cues combine to convey persuasive messages. We study persuasive technique detection in Ukrainian memes using vision-language models (VLMs). In the unconditional setting without node features, an equivariant denoiser trained on a single graph is able to generate novel graphs and sample-level metrics such as edge overlap and WL kernel similarity find no evidence of memorization. nodes.title: FORTE: A Production Framework for Feature Evaluation and Deprecation in Industrial Recommender Systems
nodes.abstract: Production recommender systems have feature-lifecycle asymmetry: adding new features must produce gains on some metric, while feature removal must not regress any metric. nodes.title: Same Query, Different Answer: Run-to-Run Variance in Semantic Query Processing
nodes.abstract: Semantic query engines ask a large language model (LLM) to judge individual rows, and benchmarks compare these engines on the quality of a few executions at temperature 0. nodes.title: MC-EvoBench: Auditing Experience-Driven Self-Improvement in Minecraft Agents
nodes.abstract: A central challenge in embodied recursive self-improvement is enabling agents to convert interaction history into capabilities that persist beyond one world and transfer to later tasks. nodes.title: SpatialASM: Internalizing Active Mentalization for Spatial Reasoning
nodes.abstract: When solving complex spatial reasoning tasks, ordinary humans naturally revisit the scenes from task-relevant viewpoints and mentally reconstruct the spatial layouts from those viewpoints. But can Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) proactively think in the same way? nodes.title: Studying Comics at Scale with Artificial Intelligence: The PAGE Framework and Three Studies of American Comics and Japanese Manga
nodes.abstract: Comics are one of the great visual records of the twentieth century: hundreds of thousands of pages in which a mass readership saw its leaders, its wars and its heroes. Most of this record has never been studied as a whole; comics scholarship proceeds one book at a time. We argue that artificial intelligence, including generative models, can change this to the benefit of the medium itself. We propose PAGE, a framewor...
nodes.delta: [Image • Visual] We demonstrate the framework on 3,929 American comic books (1938--1956) and 87 volumes of Japanese manga, in three studies, each resting on a different capability.

nodes.title: X-AgentRed: Red-Teaming Personal Agents in Evolving Multi-Service Ecosystems
nodes.abstract: Personal agents increasingly connect to services across the web and applications by using tools. As the effects of their actions accumulate and interact across services, unintended or harmful outcomes can arise when agents fulfill benign user requests. nodes.title: RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics
nodes.abstract: As AI agents increasingly rely on external tools, accurate retrieval is essential for reliable behavior. Existing methods optimize semantic relevance but largely ignore tool availability during execution. To address this gap, we propose RATED (Reliability-Aware Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics), a retrieval framework that combines robust semantic matching with dynamic reliability adaptation. nodes.title: Task Context Shapes Component Roles in Language Models
nodes.abstract: Large language models reuse the same attention heads across tasks, but identifying these shared heads does not explain what they do differently in each task. Here, we compare fixed model components across tasks using identical graph facts, statements specifying which ...

nodes.title: Revisiting Tabular Deep Regression: Objectives and the Limits of Global Early Stopping
nodes.abstract: While deep learning models for tabular data have recently received significant research attention, the choice of objective functions for regression tasks remains an understudied degree of freedom. Several lines of research offer alternatives to the standard Mean Squared Error (MSE), but differences in datasets, backbones, and evaluation protocols make their practical benefits difficult to compare. nodes.title: Next-Concept Modeling: Fast, Parallel Coarse-to-Fine Text Generation
nodes.abstract: Diffusion language models (DLMs) offer parallel sampling for faster generation than autoregressive models, an increasingly important advantage as inference becomes a dominant computational workload. However, DLMs degrade quickly with fewer sampling steps, process the full sequence at every step, and require many passes over the dataset to reach good quality. nodes.title: Hide and Seek: HIDE Concepts to SEEK explanations for black box models
nodes.abstract: Interpreting machine learning model predictions is a central challenge, particularly for black-box vision models. They require access to model weights or large concept-annotated datasets, and most methods cannot provide image-level attribution....

nodes.title: Can Language Models Play the Wikipedia Game?
nodes.abstract: Language models increasingly support or automate information retrieval from document collections too large to index. nodes.title: Do you "see" what I "see"? A Multi-panel Visual Question Answer Dataset for Large Language Model Chart Analysis
nodes.abstract: Digital libraries increasingly host scientific publications whose figures encode primary research findings, yet making this visual content searchable, accessible, and reusable remains an open challenge. nodes.title: Unconstrained CTI-REALM with Open-Weights
nodes.abstract: Organisations that want language-model agents for security work face a choice between open-weight models, which they can run and audit themselves, and far more expensive closed frontier models. We study that choice on CTI-REALM (arXiv:2603.13517), a benchmark in which an agent turns a threat-intelligence report into a working detection by querying a live telemetry store. nodes.delta: [Information • Risk] Because the benchmark's checkpoint scores largely record what an agent did or mentioned, we also introduce stage-level metrics that score what the agent submits, by executing its detection queries in the telemetry store and judging its outputs against the answer key.

nodes.title: Visualizing the World Model in an Agent's Value Function
nodes.abstract: Could model-free reinforcement learning algorithms actually be learning a model of the environment? In this work, we apply counterfactual interventions which hold everything about a state fixed, besides a targeted change, to explore if the value function of a Proximal Policy Optimization agent forms a world model of the Crafter environment. Despite only being trained to optimize reward, we discover that the value fun...
nodes.delta: [Reinforcement • Reward] Finally, we discuss the safety implications of our visualizations and some shortcomings of current reinforcement learning agents that will prevent us from building truly advanced machine intelligence.

nodes.title: Cross-Modal Latent Influence: Patch-Level Training Sample Attribution for Vision-Language Models
nodes.abstract: Explaining a vision--language model (VLM) prediction requires tracing training-example influence to the multimodal evidence that mediates it, yet existing attribution methods largely operate only at the sample level. nodes.delta: [Image • Visual] We introduce MOSAIC (Multimodal Orthogonalized Sparse Autoencoders for Influence Characterization).

nodes.title: Should SLMs be in the Driver's Seat? A Study of Local Models as Interpreters in Cloud-Written Agent Programs
nodes.abstract: The most accurate agents executing user-provided tasks are driven by large, cloud-hosted models, which solve them by reading the private data of the user. Agents powered by models small enough to run on edge devices keep that data local, but yield far worse results. nodes.title: Cortex: Measurement-Gated Evolution and Pruning of Coding-Agent Skills and Rules
nodes.abstract: Coding agents such as Claude Code also follow text files that developers write for them: a project file, skills the agent may choose to open, and rules that load automatically when the agent reads matching files. nodes.title: Learnable Low-Rank Polynomial Sketch for Effective Linear Attention
nodes.abstract: Softmax attention in Transformers suffers from quadratic complexity in sequence length, making it impractical for long-context applications. nodes.title: Harness^2: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World
nodes.abstract: LLM agents' capabilities depend not only on their underlying models but also on their execution harnesses. nodes.title: CAPTOR: a vision-language foundation model for Chest-Abdomen-Pelvis Oncologic CT
nodes.abstract: Purpose : To develop and evaluate CAPTOR, a deep-learning vision-language foundation model for oncologic chest-abdomen-pelvis (CAP) CT interpretation. nodes.title: Recycle only when you have to!
nodes.abstract: AlphaFold 3-like models (e.g., Boltz, Protenix, etc.) have pushed the frontier of protein binder design. This architecture is used both for the generation of binder candidates (e.g., by hallucination or converting these models into backbone or full atom generative models) as well as for the screening of these candidates for valid binders. nodes.title: Latent World Action Model for GUI Agents
nodes.abstract: Pixel-space world models have recently emerged as a promising approach for GUI agents, predicting future screens prior to execution and subsequently re-perceiving them for action selection. nodes.title: Agentic Data Engineering for LLMs: System Design and a Controlled Empirical Study
nodes.abstract: LLM data engineering requires iterative experimentation to determine how data selection, rewards, and curricula affect model learning, making it a natural setting for AI-for-AI (AI4AI) research. nodes.title: Akule: Fast and Scalable Multi-Robot Motion Planning via Sparse Interaction Diffusion
nodes.abstract: Diffusion models provide expressive trajectory priors for multi-robot motion planning (MRMP), but scaling them to large teams requires coordinating individual motions without expensive joint computation. nodes.title: Echo: Error-Compensated 4-Bit Tensor-Parallel Communication for LLM Training and Inference
nodes.abstract: Tensor parallelism ends every layer with an all-reduce that sits between two dependent matrix multiplications, so its cost cannot be hidden and grows as compute outpaces interconnect bandwidth. nodes.title: The RNN Homunculus: Learning to Gate Long-Term Memory
nodes.abstract: Learning long-range dependencies with recurrent neural networks (RNNs) is difficult because of the vanishing gradient problem. nodes.title: GeoFix: Geometry Fixing for 4D Consistent Generation

nodes.abstract: Recent Speech Full-Duplex (FDX) models are capable of engaging in naturalistic conversation by listening and speaking at the same time. nodes.title: MvFFN: Multi-view Floor plan Feed-forward Network for Unposed Wide-Baseline Panorama Layout Reconstruction

nodes.title: Jevolution: A Framework for Studying Communication and Collective Dynamics in AI Agents
nodes.abstract: Experiments with remote decision-making agents depend on more than the policy: the world may change during inference, the simulator determines which actions are available, and births and immigration alter who can act. nodes.delta: [Evolution • Self] We present Jevolution, an instrumented spatial predator-prey framework that makes these dependencies explicit.

nodes.title: Co-adaptive Rule Routing and Constraining for Structured Knowledge Retrieval
nodes.abstract: Structured knowledge retrieval acquires task-relevant evidence from structured knowledge sources for downstream tasks. Existing methods rely on unconstrained retrieval or predefined query-rule supervision, such as author-paper rules for scientific discovery and anatomy-drug rules for precision medicine. nodes.delta: [Safety • Memory] Experiments on STaRK-QA datasets across scientific discovery, biomedical reasoning, and e-commerce knowledge management demonstrate CoRE's effectiveness.

nodes.title: Diffusion-Based Auctions for Multi-Winner Banner Ads
nodes.abstract: We propose a new framework for banner ad auctions, leveraging diffusion models to allow for multiple bidders to co-win a single banner ad opportunity, and in particular influence the ad shown on the banner depending on the strength of their bids, enabling a far richer outcome space compared to standard banner ad auctions, where there is a single winner who shows their ad. nodes.delta: [Knowledge • Text] Extensive experimentation evaluates our proposed mechanism around the following axes: (1) efficiency improvements of our allocation rule relative to the single-winner allocation rule; (2) monotonicity of our allocation rule; and (3) approximate incentive compatibility when combining our allocation rule with Myerson lemma-based or Clarke rule-based payments.

nodes.title: RES-MR: Risk-Aware Reasoning for Explainable and Safe Medication Recommendation
nodes.abstract: Medication recommendations seek to deliver personalized drug combinations based on patients' clinical information, where ensuring transparent decision-making and personalized safety are of paramount importance. However, existing approaches predominantly operate as ``black boxes'', offering limited interpretability and hindering clinician trust. Furthermore, they typically rely on fixed, patient-agnostic safety constr...
nodes.delta: [Clinical • Medical] Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that RES-MR significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in terms of accuracy, safety, and explainability.

nodes.title: Scale, Drivers, and Limits of Representational Alignment Across Large Language Models
nodes.abstract: Comparing large language models can reveal shared representational structure and systematic differences between them. However, aggregate similarity measures can obscure how agreement varies across geometric scales and which linguistic properties support it. nodes.title: What Counts as the Same Task? Executable Contracts for Robustness Evaluation of Tool-Using Agents
nodes.abstract: Robustness tests for tool-using agents often change the agent's environment, for example by hiding a hostile note in an invoice, and then judge the agent by what it does. nodes.delta: [Code • Skill] We propose executable task contracts.

nodes.title: AphaVoice: Text-to-Speech Model for Aphasia Patient Simulation
nodes.abstract: While language therapy is the primary treatment for post-stroke aphasia, limited clinical resources often restrict patient access to proper care. nodes.title: A Controlled LLM Workflow for Evidence-Grounded Diagnosis of Risk Score Differences
nodes.abstract: We propose a controlled Large Language Model (LLM) workflow for explaining risk score differences using similar historical transactions. nodes.delta: [Safety • Memory] We propose a controlled Large Language Model (LLM) workflow for explaining risk score differences using similar historical transactions.

nodes.title: AlignPoison: Conditional Targeted Poisoning of Generative Recommenders via Decoding-Aligned Prefixes
nodes.abstract: Generative recommendation models based on autoregressive decoding have been adopted as alternatives to classical ranking-based systems. nodes.title: HiPPT: Physiology-Grounded Wearable PPG Representation Learning via Multi-Scope Text Alignment
nodes.abstract: Reusable wearable PPG representations should capture local pulse morphology and broader physiological regularities. nodes.title: Reels-RSI: Program-Level Self-Improvement for Code-Rendered Explainer Videos
nodes.abstract: Explainer videos -- a worked geometry problem, why the sky is blue, how a dynasty fell -- are usually one more target for pixel video generation. We argue they are a different kind of artifact: a program (script, storyboard and per-frame animation code) that a deterministic renderer turns into frames. nodes.title: Rethinking Activation Functions: Reducing Bias Can Improve Learning
nodes.abstract: Many widely used activation functions, including ReLU, GELU, Swish, and Sigmoid, produce predominantly positive outputs, resulting in a nonzero post-activation mean that we term activation bias. nodes.title: MontageFlow: Physically Valid High Fidelity EEG Generation
nodes.abstract: Generative modeling offers a promising solution to the scarcity of labeled clinical electroencephalography (EEG) data under strict privacy constraints. nodes.abstract: Multi-robot systems (MRS) offer significant advantages over single-robot platforms by enabling information sharing and coordination for different tasks in complex environments. nodes.title: FDE-Bench: Evaluating End-to-End Delivery from Underspecified Real-World Business Requests

nodes.abstract: Emerging strong Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have advanced navigation foundation models. nodes.title: Are Multimodal Benchmarks Really Useful? Item-Level Multimodal Benchmark Diagnosis via Structure-Response Co-Calibration
nodes.abstract: Multimodal benchmarks are central to evaluating whether models can reason over information from multiple modalities. nodes.title: A Self-Defining Operator for Distributed Applications
nodes.abstract: To operate distributed applications with high availability, operators must rapidly diagnose and mitigate any incident. nodes.abstract: Physical systems and distributed AI workflows can retain past information, receive delayed feedback and combine conflicting signals. nodes.abstract: Dynamic Product Advertising (DPA) retrieval systems are a core component of modern e-commerce advertising; however, their evaluation remains challenging. nodes.abstract: Protocol specifications rarely justify executable behavior in one place: a transition may inherit its source state from a remote control block, name its events only by number, and remain subject to a later correction. nodes.title: PsyMemBehav: Psychology-Informed and Memory-Grounded Two-Level Identity-to-Action Reasoning for Social-Media Behavior Simulation
nodes.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) support social simulation, but faithfully reproducing real users requires grounding both structured platform decisions and language in sparse, noisy behavioral evidence. nodes.title: MHWA: Multi-timescale Hierarchical World-Action Model
nodes.abstract: Autoregressive world models have emerged as a powerful paradigm for sample efficient decision making, yet their open loop rollouts often exhibit increasing drift that leads to error accumulation even within a relatively small planning horizon. Hierarchical temporal abstraction is a natural candidate to mitigate such drift by reducing the effective prediction horizon; however, existing hierarchical designs can introdu...
nodes.delta: [Manipulation • Action] Empirically, using RLiable's seed-by-game aggregation, MHWA (77M parameters) achieves an IQM human normalized score (HNS) of 0.884 across three training seeds on a 14-game Atari subset using 10% subsampled offline data, outperforming a matched JOWA-70M baseline (0.529) and achieving numerically comparable performance to JOWA-150M while using nearly half the parameters and 70.88% fewer training FLOPs per sequence.

nodes.title: Self-improving data synthesis can scale embedding-model adaptation across domains and tasks
nodes.abstract: AI agents require specialised retrieval across domains and tasks, but adapting embedding models is constrained by costly manual training-data design. Here we introduce SYNTRA, a self-improving agentic data synthesis framework that turns a few retrieval examples into reusable synthesis instructions. Given an unlabelled corpus and a few relevant query-document pairs, SYNTRA infers implicit information needs and relevan...
nodes.delta: [Safety • Memory] Experiments across 24 datasets spanning 15 domains demonstrate that the same synthesis workflow produces effective training data, benefiting even strong embedding models with and without existing labelled training sets.

nodes.title: Think in Strategies, Act with Tools: Traceable Agentic Optimization for Combinatorial Problems
nodes.abstract: Optimization by PROmpting (OPRO) directly leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate candidate solutions through natural-language prompting. However, OPRO's optimization process is difficult to track, which prevents LLMs from capturing useful information accumulated over previous iterations, thereby limiting solution quality. To address this limitation, we propose a Tool-Augmented Strategic Agent (TASA) which...
nodes.delta: [Evolution • Self] Moreover, we leverage LLM to construct problem-specific tools and introduce a strategy-guided adaptive tool planner, which efficiently utilizes the information of trajectory to update solutions.

nodes.title: PTGPO: Prefix Tree Group Policy Optimization
nodes.abstract: Training language agents on long-horizon interactive tasks is challenging because sparse terminal rewards provide weak credit signals for intermediate actions. Existing group-based methods either assign a shared trajectory-level advantage or estimate step-level advantages from state groups, which may conflate the current action with subsequent decisions. We propose Prefix Tree Group Policy Optimization (PTGPO), a cri...
nodes.delta: [Reinforcement • Reward] We propose Prefix Tree Group Policy Optimization (PTGPO), a critic-free method that constructs prefix trees over trajectory suffixes within anchor-state groups.

nodes.title: SAGE: Pushing 2-Bit Vector-Quantized LLMs toward Real-World Usability
nodes.abstract: Extreme low-bit weight-only quantization is an effective approach to reducing the deployment costs of large language models. Below 3 bits, scalar quantization often suffers severe accuracy loss, while vector quantization (VQ) better preserves accuracy through more expressive joint encoding. However, existing VQ methods still exhibit substantial degradation on real-world tasks, and two design challenges remain underex...
nodes.delta: [Image • Visual] Across benchmarks covering knowledge, mathematics, code generation, instruction following, and tool use, SAGE achieves state-of-the-art performance in the 2-bit quantization setting.

nodes.title: Equal-information evaluation of credit assignment in modular financial reinforcement learning
nodes.abstract: Credit assignment in modular financial reinforcement learning is difficult to evaluate because an attributed signal may improve a component loss without adding decision-relevant information or improving economic outcomes. We propose an evaluation framework combining equal-information reconstruction controls, fixed-utility comparisons and prespecified downstream guardrails. The framework is instantiated in an attribut...
nodes.delta: [Reinforcement • Reward] These results identify three distinct evaluation failures: redundant attribution signals, representation-induced prediction trade-offs, and misalignment between component supervision and downstream risk outcomes.

nodes.title: GateSight: Recurrent Memory Anticipates Attention Memory for Query-Agnostic KV Eviction in Hybrid LLMs
nodes.abstract: Hybrid language models interleave Gated DeltaNet (GDN) layers, whose recurrent memory has a fixed size, with full-attention layers, whose key-value (KV) cache grows with the context and dominates serving memory. In this paper, we ask whether the recurrent memory already knows what the attention memory will need. nodes.delta: [Graph • Diffusion] Because the relation is spread across many GDN heads and layers, and a linear map recovers its trend but less of its high-utility tail than a nonlinear one, we propose GateSight, which learns it with lightweight per-head multilayer perceptrons that read these signals and no attention score.

nodes.title: CUSE: Fine-Grained Multimodal Unlearning with Counterfactual Guidance and On-Policy Self-Distillation
nodes.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can reproduce sensitive, copyrighted, or unsafe information from their training data. Effective unlearning must remove target information while preserving non-target content, even within the same response. nodes.delta: [Clinical • Medical] We propose CUSE, a Counterfactual-guided Unlearning framework via on-policy Self-distillation for multimodal large language models.

nodes.title: Last Secure Code Benchmark: Is the Code You Vibe Secure?
nodes.abstract: AI coding agents now write much of the code that ships, yet whether that code is secure remains unclear. We introduce the Last Secure Code Benchmark, a comprehensive evaluation of secure code generation by coding agents. Built from 150 real vulnerabilities, its 450 tasks span seven widely used languages (Java, C, C++, JavaScript, Python, PHP, and Go), 24 CWEs including 21 of the 2025 CWE Top 25 and 8 of the Top 10 KE...
nodes.delta: [Code • Skill] We introduce the Last Secure Code Benchmark, a comprehensive evaluation of secure code generation by coding agents.

nodes.title: Prior-Fitted and Frozen Scorers for Multimodal Contrastive Learning
nodes.abstract: Multimodal contrastive learning typically relies on manually specified scoring functions, such as cosine similarity, to quantify the similarity between representations from different modalities. Several such functions have been recently proposed to extend contrastive learning beyond two modalities. In principle, however, any function that assigns high compatibility to matched samples and low compatibility to mismatch...
nodes.delta: [Image • Visual] Building on this observation, we introduce the Prior-Fitted Scorer (PFS): a Transformer scorer pre-trained on synthetic multimodal data generated from structural causal model (SCM) priors before transferring it to real-world data.

nodes.title: How Should a Camera-First AI Agent Work?
nodes.abstract: Camera-first agents must act on the visual world as it unfolds. We argue that the central obstacle for future camera-first agents is not recognition ability - multimodal models (vision-language and live/streaming alike) generalize well through language and remain the right tool for semantic reasoning - but time. nodes.title: ProgAgent: Learning Tool Orchestration through Programmatic Training
nodes.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly expected to orchestrate diverse tools over long-horizon tasks. Existing agents typically use Direct Tool Calling (DTC), where the model invokes tools sequentially, and tool responses accumulate in the model context, which can lead to context rot and orchestration breakdown. In contrast, Programmatic Tool Calling (PTC) invokes tools through executable code and stores inter...
nodes.delta: [Evolution • Self] Cross-harness experiments show that PTC-trained models outperform DTC-trained models under both evaluation interfaces, suggesting that the benefits of PTC training extend beyond the interface.

nodes.title: Training a Compact, Strong, and Realistic Text-to-Speech Model
nodes.abstract: Text-to-speech (TTS) systems are conventionally optimized for intelligibility and speaker similarity. However, neither objective captures the prosodic detail that distinguishes human performances from synthetic speech, leaving a realism gap that larger models and higher-quality data can narrow but not close. In the absence of an objective that directly targets this gap, realism remains a persistent challenge in TTS. ...
nodes.delta: [Knowledge • Text] We present Audio8-TTS, a compact 0.6B-parameter model for zero-shot voice cloning that achieves state-of-the-art performance in intelligibility and speaker similarity, with particularly strong results in perceptual naturalness.

nodes.title: LYNX: Analytical Program Synthesis via Grounding and Closed-Loop Refinement
nodes.abstract: LLM-powered data analytics aims to translate natural language instructions into executable analytical programs over underlying data. nodes.title: Counterfactual Regret for Reflective Agents with Lean-Verified Guarantees
nodes.abstract: Reflective language agents reuse feedback and memory to adapt across tasks without updating model weights. However, existing guarantees for policy selection and action generation do not by themselves establish when local reflection yields long-term performance guarantees for the complete agent under resource constraints. nodes.title: GREAT-ESDD: Graph Edge Attention Network for Effectively Steered Delivery Decisions
nodes.abstract: Online, same-day delivery requires operators to constantly update their routes, and the routing cost for deliveries increases with the number of customers. Out-of-home (OOH) delivery options can help companies handle increasing customer numbers while keeping delivery costs low. nodes.title: CESNET-TimeSeries26: A Multi-Year Network Traffic Time Series Dataset for Annual Seasonality, Concept Drift, and Long-Term Anomaly Detection
nodes.abstract: Forecast-based models are fundamental to network traffic management and anomaly detection. However, it is essential to evaluate these forecasting models over extended periods of time in order to assess their adaptability to unexpected phenomena and shifts in underlying patterns. nodes.title: YOUDrive: Driving Style as a Composable Direction for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
nodes.abstract: End-to-end driving policies can achieve strong task performance while offering limited control over their driving style. Driving style describes how a vehicle accelerates, brakes, and maintains distance. Policies trained without explicit preference conditioning lack a direct mechanism for adjusting these behaviors at inference. nodes.title: ASIWorld: Benchmarking Autonomous Agents in a Persistent Survival Sandbox
nodes.abstract: Evaluating autonomous agents requires examining whether they can translate goals into coherent action across extended interactions. In persistent environments, this requires coordinating interdependent actions under incomplete observations, accounting for delayed effects, and adapting as earlier decisions shape subsequent opportunities. nodes.title: Depth-progressive 3D seismic velocity model building via 2D generative diffusion models
nodes.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) velocity model building (VMB) remains computationally challenging with conventional approaches and native 3D neural networks, largely due to the prohibitive memory and training cost of full 3D formulations. nodes.title: Seamless Deployment of Machine Learning Inference at the Far Edge: An Empirical AWS IoT Greengrass Architecture for Industrial Predictive Maintenance
nodes.abstract: Industrial IoT sensors produce continuous, high-volume data streams that predictive maintenance needs to analyse in real time. Cloud-centric architectures send all raw telemetry to central servers, which costs latency, bandwidth and resilience. nodes.delta: [Manipulation • Action] We deploy two configurations on real AWS infrastructure and compare them: a cloud-only baseline (Configuration A) and the proposed hybrid edge architecture (Configuration B).

nodes.title: A Reference Architecture for Integrating Agentic AI into Enterprise Software: Responsibilities, Interactions, and Variability
nodes.abstract: Agentic AI moves generative AI applications toward systems that coordinate reasoning, enterprise context, model inference, and external actions. Integrating these capabilities into enterprise software introduces diverse architectural concerns, from orchestration, knowledge and memory, and model access to tools and actions, security, runtime infrastructure, and evaluation. nodes.title: AI-Native Product Management: A Vision
nodes.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used to support product management tasks. At the same time, AI-native research and development (R&D) may increase software realization capacity. Organizations may realize software faster than they can identify, qualify, and reconsider what should be realized. nodes.title: Cross-Lingual TTS for Indian Languages: A Benchmark and Inference-Time Duration Estimation Strategies
nodes.abstract: Recent alignment-free Text-to-Speech (TTS) models achieve high synthesis quality by removing explicit alignment modules and simplifying training. However, they often struggle in cross-lingual scenarios due to differences in character durations across languages, leading to duration mismatch and degraded speech quality. nodes.title: EvoCowork: A Benchmark for Real-World Office Tasks
nodes.abstract: Office workflows are a demanding testbed for self-improving agents because their deliverables must be correct, natively editable, and mutually consistent. A central question is whether gains on feedback tasks reflect reusable procedures rather than task-specific fixes. nodes.abstract: Claims of recursive self-improvement are easy to make and hard to falsify: did improvement come from re-using designer-provided mechanisms, or from mechanisms the system authored itself? nodes.title: Getting Space Right: Agentic Rewards for Image Generation
nodes.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is promising for spatial text-to-image generation, but existing work largely focuses on policy optimization, assuming accurate rewards and effective online rollouts. nodes.title: PEAM: On-device Communication Agent for Personalized, Efficient and Autonomous Mobile Network Configuration
nodes.abstract: The growing deployment of compact large language models on smartphones is enabling autonomous on-device decision-making, such as emerging mobile GUI agents. However, many mobile decisions, such as network configuration when users switch apps or connectivity conditions change, must satisfy stringent latency constraints to preserve user experience. In this paper, we propose PEAM, an on-device LLM-based communication ag...

nodes.title: WeatherBridge: Forecast-Aware Multi-Source Input Adaptation for Pretrained Weather Forecasting Models
nodes.abstract: Data-driven weather forecasting models are commonly trained on ERA5, yet operational deployment must use timely initial states from physics-based numerical weather prediction (NWP) systems whose distributions differ substantially from ERA5. nodes.title: Beyond Outcome Feedback: Trajectory-Quality-Guided Experience-based Learning
nodes.abstract: Experience-based learning enables large language model (LLM) agents to improve over time by reusing knowledge from past executions. However, existing methods typically rely on final task outcomes as feedback for experience learning, overlooking the execution process and limiting their ability to evaluate and optimize experience based on trajectory quality. To address this limitation, we propose TQG-Exp, a trajectory-...

nodes.title: MARL-BattleGrounds: A Novel JAX-native Benchmark for Heterogeneous and Competitive Multi-agent RL
nodes.abstract: We present MARL-BattleGrounds (MARL-BGs), an easy-to-use JAX-native benchmark for heterogeneous and competitive multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), designed to be sample-efficient, computationally efficient, and researcher-centric. nodes.title: Probable but Not Valid: A Psychometric Audit of Decision Models as Synthetic Survey Respondents
nodes.abstract: Language models are increasingly used to create synthetic survey samples, also called silicon samples. Decision models are a new class of language models that return a probability for each point of a rating scale instead of text. nodes.title: Bridging Risk Approximation Gaps in Model Predictive Task Sampling via In-Context Modeling
nodes.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is essential for adaptive decision-making, e.g., robust Meta-RL and domain randomization (DR), and efficient post-training of large language models (LLMs), where tasks are commonly structured as Markov decision processes or prompts. A central bottleneck in all these settings is the cost of agent-environment interactions required for task selection and policy optimization. Model predictive ...

nodes.title: WorkBorne: Discovering Agentic Tasks from Real-World Artifact Transitions
nodes.abstract: Developing terminal-based agents for long-horizon execution demands synthetic tasks that tightly couple complex instructions with authentic, interactive environments. nodes.delta: [Code • Skill] Experiments on Qwen3.5-27B and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B show that WorkBorne substantially improves over base models (i.e., improving Terminal-Bench 2.1 from 43.1% to 61.8% and ClawEval General score from 75.0 to 80.2) and achieves the strongest overall performance among other synthesis baselines (e.g., TMax (Ivison et al., 2026), RST (Li et al., 2026a), Terminal-Universe (Wu et al., 2026a)).

nodes.title: SkillForgeBench: Evaluating Agent Reliability Grounded in Agent Skill Specifications
nodes.abstract: Evaluating an agent's ability to strictly satisfy diverse and procedurally complex requirements is essential to determining its practical reliability. Conducting such an evaluation demands agentic tasks that reconcile broad domain coverage with deep procedural complexity. nodes.delta: [Code • Skill] To resolve this tension, we present SkillForgeBench, which leverages agent skills as unifying execution blueprints across three co-designed stages: (1) Resource Preparation uses domain-balanced skills to guide artifact retrieval, establishing broad workflow coverage; (2) Skill-driven Task Synthesis employs skills as procedural anchors to partition artifact roles, synthesize naturalistic task instructions, and package sandboxed scenarios for deep procedural execution; and (3) Holistic Evaluation Design translates skill-embedded requirements into fine-grained completion and process rubrics to enable strict requirement-level scoring.

nodes.title: Predicting how model propensities generalize out of distribution
nodes.abstract: How do language models generalize from their training data? This is a central challenge for alignment: models reliably learn their training distribution given enough samples, but we want models that behave well when deployed in new contexts. nodes.title: VC-OPD: Visual Counterfactual On-Policy Distillation for Grounded Vision-Language Reasoning
nodes.abstract: GRPO-style reinforcement learning has advanced vision-language reasoning, but its sequence-level rewards provide limited credit assignment for individual reasoning tokens.
