nodes.abstract: In this work, we evaluate a simple inference-time scaling approach based on \textit{turn-level best-of-N sampling} (\method) for large language model (LLM) agents on complex, long-horizon tasks. We instantiate this using a \textit{generator-selector} framework with two LLMs; at each turn, a \emph{generator} model generates [MATH] candidate actions and a \emph{selector} model selects one of them, which is then execute...
nodes.delta: [Evolution • Self] Analysis of agent trajectories reveal a shift in agent behaviour towards desirable patterns such as reduction in number of attempts to solve the task, improved task instruction following, debugging and testing.

nodes.title: Learning to Decode Linear Codes with Generalized Belief Propagation Network
nodes.abstract: Error correcting codes are a fundamental component of communication systems, enabling reliable data transmission over noisy channels. Recently, neural decoders have demonstrated notable performance gains over classical iterative algorithms. In this paper, we propose a Generalized Belief Propagation Network (GBPNet) that preserves message-passing symmetry while enhancing the decoder's learning capability. The architec...
nodes.delta: [Image • Visual] Experimental results on several linear codes show that GBPNet achieves lower bit error rates than conventional belief propagation and the evaluated state-of-the-art neural decoders.

nodes.title: Autonomous AI Agents Systematically Diverge From Human Preferences in Proof Formalization
nodes.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems have ushered in a new age of proof abundance, but helping humans understand these proofs requires new attention to the differences in how AI agents and humans pursue a proof-making task. We present "simulated collaboration", a methodology that allows us to examine two key questions: (1) the relative attention AI agents pay to surface syntax or, conversely, deeper underlying semant...
nodes.delta: [Code • Skill] We present "simulated collaboration", a methodology that allows us to examine two key questions: (1) the relative attention AI agents pay to surface syntax or, conversely, deeper underlying semantics, and (2) how and where AI agent preferences for what to do next diverge from human preferences.

nodes.title: Dull, Dirty, Dangerous? Working Conditions and the Limits of Occupational AI Exposure
nodes.abstract: Automation is often justified as relief from dull, dirty, and dangerous work. I examine how these conditions relate to occupational AI exposure using 21 O*NET items across 754 US occupations. Higher exposure is associated with lower condition scores under a large language model (LLM) measure and AI Occupational Exposure (AIOE), with equal occupation weights and employment weights. Adjustment for physical demands, req...
nodes.delta: [Safety • Memory] Establishing desired automation or realized relief requires evidence about workers' preferences and specific interventions.

nodes.title: Trust Responsive Runtime Authorization for Agentic AI with Empirical Characterization of Policy Behavior and Parameter Sensitivity
nodes.abstract: The policy that converts runtime estimates of an autonomous agent's condition into operational authority is rarely specified or measured. We empirically characterize the Trust Responsive Authorization Policy (TRAP), which maps an Authorization Readiness Score (ARS), a weighted combination of runtime trust, operational stability, and contextual risk, onto discrete authorization levels through an asymmetric rule: escal...
nodes.delta: [Information • Risk] All reported values are traceable to the publicly available, versioned research release.

nodes.title: Occlusion for Free: Detecting Occlusion from the Disagreement Between Two Monocular Distance Cues
nodes.abstract: Knowing that a pedestrian is occluded is useful to a robot even when the detector cannot recover the hidden pixels, but occlusion estimators are normally trained on occlusion annotations that deployment settings rarely have. We show that occlusion can be read off two distance estimates a camera-only pipeline already computes. Apparent height is largely unchanged by occlusion, because the detected box still spans the ...
nodes.delta: [World • Forecasting] Signals that need no local annotation are worth more in settings that benchmarks do not represent.

nodes.title: Perceptive Humanoid Motion from Simulation
nodes.abstract: Humanoid robots have the potential to automate a wide range of physical tasks. Progress toward generalist humanoid autonomy, however, remains constrained by a data bottleneck: mapping pixels and free-form language to low-level joint commands requires paired supervision, and no corpus of such data exists at sufficiently large scale. Some approaches rely on human teleoperation and wearable capture devices, which requir...
nodes.delta: [Manipulation • Action] We present HALO, a humanoid autonomy system powered by a pipeline that synthesizes vision-language-motion data across a thousand procedurally generated homes.

nodes.title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
nodes.abstract: AI agents are playing an increasingly important role in physics research. However, existing physics benchmarks only evaluate fixed questions, isolated sub-tasks, or paper reproduction with given solutions, and rarely check research quality alongside correctness. We introduce FrontierPhysics, an end-to-end benchmark with 56 tasks made by 42 physicists based on their own research, covering nine domains across theoretic...
nodes.delta: [Code • Skill] We introduce FrontierPhysics, an end-to-end benchmark with 56 tasks made by 42 physicists based on their own research, covering nine domains across theoretical, computational, and experimental physics.

nodes.title: BEAKER: An Expert-Curated Benchmark for Embodied Brains in Self-Driving Chemical Laboratories
nodes.abstract: Self-Driving Chemical Laboratories (SDCLs) are moving chemical experimentation toward embodied automation, where machines must perceive laboratory scenes, reason about experimental states, and act under physical, procedural, and safety constraints. Although Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are increasingly considered as embodied brains for such systems, existing laboratory benchmarks mainly focus on safety, a...
nodes.delta: [Evolution • Self] To fill this gap, we introduce BEAKER, a Benchmark for evaluating Embodied Actionability, Knowledge, Experimentation, and Reasoning in SDCLs.

nodes.title: Adapting the Process of Adaptation: Darwinian, Lamarckian, and Agent-Directed Evolution in AI
nodes.abstract: Evolution has shaped intelligence for billions of years. Artificial intelligence (AI) now raises a striking possibility: intelligence may begin to direct its own evolution. As AI agents become capable of modifying and evaluating their own behavior, how quickly could they improve, and how can that improvement remain safe? We develop a theoretical framework comparing Darwinian, Lamarckian, and agent-directed evolution ...
nodes.delta: [Evolution • Self] The central challenge is not simply to accelerate the evolution of intelligence, but to preserve humanity's ability to guide its direction, limit its speed, and intervene when necessary.

nodes.title: Closed-Loop Agent Evaluation: Layered Measurement and Self-Calibration
nodes.abstract: Once an agent is live, teams want to know whether it is doing its job, not just whether it throws errors. Yet most evaluation is one-off: a benchmark run, a look at traces, a single score. Its conclusions neither check themselves nor reach the agent. We propose closed-loop evaluation, an evaluation method for deployed agents. It models evaluation as performance estimation under biased raters and censored outcomes, an...
nodes.delta: [Information • Risk] We propose closed-loop evaluation, an evaluation method for deployed agents.

nodes.title: Reclassification Is All You Missed: Surfacing Variant Reinterpretation Need in Online Health Communities at Population Scale
nodes.abstract: Genetic variants are routinely reclassified in ClinVar after a patient is tested, sometimes from uncertain to pathogenic, yet patient recontact is inconsistent, with no clear duty and responsibility diffused among labs, providers, and patients. Many affected people discuss their results in public online health communities that clinical recontact often does not reach. We built PRISM, an agentic large-language-model pi...
nodes.delta: [Clinical • Medical] PRISM contributes a population-scale reinterpretation-need map with code and data to be released upon publication.

nodes.title: Segment What It Can Draw: Querying a Text-to-Image Generator with Its Own Images for Skin Lesion Segmentation
nodes.abstract: Skin lesion segmentation without annotated masks requires the target to be specified through other cues. Existing approaches rely on dermoscopy-specific rules, annotation-derived model priors, or user-selected regions. A general text-to-image diffusion transformer offers a text interface to the target, but its concept-word attention is unreliable on dermoscopy images: in the model's attention-output space, the word-d...
nodes.delta: [Clinical • Medical] It outperforms zero-shot and word-based attention methods on all three sets, and a hand-designed dermoscopy pipeline in Dice and IoU on two.

nodes.title: SD-LoRA: Training-Time Structural Distillation into LoRA for Few-Shot Vision-Language Adaptation
nodes.abstract: Few-shot adaptation of vision-language models must balance two competing goals: learning fine-grained visual distinctions from very limited supervision and preserving the efficiency that makes frozen CLIP-like models attractive for deployment. Existing lightweight adaptation methods, including prompt tuning, LoRA, and cache-based adapters, typically supervise global image embeddings and therefore underuse token-level...
nodes.delta: [Image • Visual] Rather than retaining this graph at test time, SD-LoRA transfers its structural bias into the shared CLIP-LoRA backbone through implicit distillation and Prototype Predictive Alignment, which aligns graph-conditioned representations with support-derived class prototypes.

nodes.title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning via Epigraph-Form Guided Exploration
nodes.abstract: Discovering cooperative behavior in multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is challenging due to the combinatorial complexity of joint state-action spaces, which hinders the emergence of coordinated behaviors from trial-and-error alone. Intrinsic rewards are often used to aid discovery, but naively combining them with team objectives can distort the learning signal, compromising task performance. In this paper, we...
nodes.delta: [Reinforcement • Reward] Empirically, our method outperforms strong baselines and induces novel cooperative strategies across SMAX, VMAS, and MPE benchmark suites.

nodes.title: Finite-Time Convergence and Regret Guarantees for Neural Reinforcement Learning in POMDPs
nodes.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) in Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes (POMDPs) is computationally challenging due to the curse of long-range dependence on history. Fortunately, recent studies have shown that a range of POMDPs that satisfy the filter stability assumption can be well approximated by a superstate Markov Decision Process (MDP) based on a truncated history in a finite-memory window, with a value g...
nodes.delta: [Reinforcement • Reward] Our numerical experiments also verify our theoretical results.

nodes.title: Shaping & Monitoring Models through their Internal Representations
nodes.abstract: We propose Mechanistic Shaping, a unified framework for shaping models through their internal representations. Mechanistic Shaping is applied during training so that models follow specifications (rules) about which concepts they express, measured via their outputs or internal representations (e.g., no harmful content), and also which concepts they rely on, i.e., what they use to make their decisions (e.g., not a cand...
nodes.delta: [Graph • Diffusion] We therefore introduce a hierarchy of such classes, which separates a concept that escapes one probe from a concept that is truly gone.

nodes.title: When Verification Is Not Agreement: Cross-Agent LLM-to-Dafny Formalization
nodes.abstract: A verified Dafny postcondition certifies that a formula holds, but it does not guarantee that the result was reached through genuine independent reasoning. We introduce a cross-agent formalization protocol where a Specifier model translates clinical trial criteria into a Dafny predicate, and an Implementer model writes an operational method checked against it. A same-model control establishes that even with no capabi...
nodes.delta: [Information • Risk] Evaluating four model configurations on 96 clinical trial documents, we find that agreement is highly sensitive to how model capability is allocated across the two roles: the GPT-4.1-nano/GPT-4.1-mini configuration achieves 53.0% agreement when the stronger model is the Implementer, but only 14.3% when the roles are reversed.

nodes.title: Synthesizing symbolic models of human and machine reasoning at scale
nodes.abstract: Symbolic models offer a powerful account of cognition, but their scope has historically been limited by the need for hand-engineering and computational tractability. We show how advances in artificial intelligence (AI) can scale symbolic modeling and help overcome these engineering limitations. We introduce Behavior-Conditioned Symbolic Synthesis (BCSS)---an approach for automated search of interpretable, determinist...
nodes.delta: [Safety • Memory] We introduce Behavior-Conditioned Symbolic Synthesis (BCSS)---an approach for automated search of interpretable, deterministic symbolic programs that verifiably reproduce behavior---and apply it to model both human and machine behavior across hundreds of challenging reasoning problems.

nodes.title: Polynomial-Time Computation of Extensive-Form Proper Equilibria in Two-Player Zero-Sum Games
nodes.abstract: We give a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for computing an exact extensive-form proper equilibrium in a finite two-player zero-sum extensive-form game with perfect recall and rational data. Properness is understood in the agent normal form: an action at an information set is penalized relative to a better action while all other local behavioral choices, including the player's own future actions, remain fixed....
nodes.delta: [Reinforcement • Reward] A scaled doubly stochastic representation embeds these restrictions in a polynomial-size sequence-form polytope; a saddle point then satisfies the local [MATH]-properness inequalities.

nodes.title: A Night at the LLM Zoo: Data Conditioned Flow Matching for Generating Pretrained LLM Weights
nodes.abstract: A challenge to Weight Space Learning as it expands from task specific and vision models to Large Language Models (LLMs) is the absence of a well curated and analyzed LLM population. To address this, we train such a model zoo for application to Weight Space Generation by systematically varying the data mixture composition between web text, books, mathematics, coding, and French across populations of 51M, 124M, and 355...
nodes.delta: [Graph • Diffusion] Finally, we produce all source code and artifacts to support the continued expansion of Weight Space Learning and Generation into the LLM domain.

nodes.title: PromptOps: Iterative Prompt Optimization for LLM-as-a-Judge Systems
nodes.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as automated judges for evaluating the behavior of chatbots and other AI systems. In deployment, however, their agreement with the intended human evaluation policy may degrade as user interactions and score distributions change. Existing automatic prompt optimization methods are primarily studied as one-shot procedures on static development sets and therefore provide...
nodes.delta: [Code • Skill] These findings establish prompt optimization for deployed LLM judges as an inherently iterative maintenance problem and demonstrate that PromptOps provides a practical abstraction for studying and implementing this process.

nodes.title: Adapting LLM Judges to Observed Human Annotation Policy through Soft Prompt Tuning
nodes.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly employed as automated judges for evaluating chatbot responses. While proprietary models can achieve high agreement with human annotators, they remain costly and difficult to deploy in practical settings. Lightweight open-source LLM judges provide an attractive alternative but typically exhibit lower agreement with human ratings. In this paper, we investigate whether soft ...
nodes.delta: [Judge • Recommender] Our findings demonstrate that hybrid soft-prompt tuning, which combines textual prompts with learned continuous prompt embeddings, consistently improves agreement with human annotations over the corresponding untuned baselines.

nodes.title: More Agents, More Reliable? System-Level Reliability of Multi-Agent LLMs under Operational-Profile Uncertainty
nodes.abstract: Teams increasingly build software from cooperating large language model (LLM) agents, often assuming more agents mean more reliability. Yet the usual evidence, average benchmark accuracy, ignores the input mix a deployed system meets and the rule merging the agents' answers. Building on HIP-LLM, a hierarchical imprecise-probability assessment of single LLMs, we propose a framework combining it with a Bayesian network...
nodes.delta: [Code • Skill] Building on HIP-LLM, a hierarchical imprecise-probability assessment of single LLMs, we propose a framework combining it with a Bayesian network of the system's failure logic for multi-agent systems.

nodes.title: Depth or Description? When a One-Step Latent Score Replaces Lookahead in Proactive Information Acquisition
nodes.abstract: A proactive agent must decide what to ask before it acts. Exact lookahead values combinations of questions but is expensive and leans on a fitted model; a one-step score is cheap but can miss them. Our main finding: the need for depth often lies in how the hidden cause is described. A one-step score on the label can be blind to an interaction among answers. A score on a suitable latent cause is not, and where that la...
nodes.delta: [Information • Risk] Probabilities learned from one language model's answers do not carry to another unless planning allows for both; those read from tokens are worth only a few labels.

nodes.title: Multi-step SWE: Can Coding Agents Keep Building on Their Own Code Over Long Horizons?
nodes.abstract: Developers rarely give a coding agent a single request: they ask it to build a component and then to extend, upgrade, and optimize it, each time on code the agent itself wrote. Most benchmarks, however, score one task at a time. We introduce Multi-step SWE, a long-horizon benchmark of 69 software engineering tasks, each a chain of 5-15 dependent steps on a single codebase. Every step is a complete, multi-hour enginee...
nodes.delta: [Code • Skill] We introduce Multi-step SWE, a long-horizon benchmark of 69 software engineering tasks, each a chain of 5-15 dependent steps on a single codebase.

nodes.title: SeVerus: Context-Aware, Gamified Benchmarking for Rust Verification
nodes.abstract: Coding agents achieve high success rates on existing benchmarks for Verus, a verifier for Rust programs. These benchmarks typically provide the auxiliary lemmas needed to complete a proof. In practice, however, such lemmas must be discovered and proved. To capture this challenge, we present SEVERUS, a context-aware technique to generate Verus benchmarks that organizes verification tasks into quests, each divided into...
nodes.delta: [Code • Skill] To capture this challenge, we present SEVERUS, a context-aware technique to generate Verus benchmarks that organizes verification tasks into quests, each divided into levelsin a gamified manner.

nodes.title: Compositional Unalignment: Auditing Safety in Large Vision-Language Models
nodes.abstract: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) are vulnerable to compositional harm: an image and a prompt that are benign in isolation become harmful through the model's cross-modal reasoning. Recent alignment methods report strong scores on compositional safety benchmarks, but an LLM judge only measures observed behavior and cannot reveal how robustly safety is integrated into the model. We argue that un-alignment provides a...
nodes.delta: [Judge • Recommender] On Qwen2.5-VL-7B and LLaVA-1.5-7B, CMaG reduces compositional safety scores by up to 65 points while over 98% of outputs remain coherent, outperforming gradient-based baselines; the direction also transfers to text-explicit harm and un-aligns models hardened by defensive training.

nodes.title: TileQuant: Tile as the Precision-Allocation Unit for LLM Mixed-Precision Post-Training Quantization
nodes.abstract: Post-training quantization (PTQ) reduces large language model (LLM) deployment costs, but preserving quality requires accounting for uneven weight sensitivity. Uniform PTQ uses one weight bit-width, importance-aware PTQ adjusts scales or reconstructs weights within that width, and column-wise mixed precision retains selected columns at higher precision. However, sensitivity varies within columns, so whole-column rete...
nodes.delta: [Image • Visual] We therefore introduce TileQuant, a training-free framework that assigns precision to hardware-aligned 2D weight tiles.

nodes.title: SPILLWAY: Separating Target Admission from Sanitization to Defend Tool-Using Agents against Prompt Injection
nodes.abstract: Tool-using agents act on email, files, and payments, so an instruction hidden in a web page or a shared document can make an agent send data or money to an attacker. Many runtime defenses put a language model on the decision that lets an action through, so the decision depends on a model that may read the attacker's text and adds model calls to every step. Provenance defenses keep the model off the final check but ne...
nodes.delta: [Information • Risk] As personal AI agents act on users' email, files, and payments, SPILLWAY gives them an auditable refusal floor on where their actions go that keeps them useful and holds across backbones.

nodes.title: Archetypal contexts in the neurons of language models: an architecture for intelligence?
nodes.abstract: We validate our previous hypothesis that a language model holds relational patterns apart from the subject domains that instantiate them (Nordfors, 2026). These archetypal contexts are patterns of relations that people recognize across many fields, such as the tipping point or winner takes all, held once and applied across domains. We show this inside the model, Qwen3.8-27B. One set of neurons carries the archetype, ...
nodes.delta: [Knowledge • Text] The neurons, the texts and the code are released with this paper as its reproduction package, so that anyone can repeat the test inside the model.

nodes.title: MAC-v2: Long-horizon model-based value expansion from pixels
nodes.abstract: We study whether \emph{long-horizon model-based value expansion} can serve as an effective framework in pixel-based offline reinforcement learning (RL). Long-horizon model-based value expansion from pixels is substantially harder than state-based environments, as the agent must learn both the representation and its dynamics, and errors from either can accumulate recursively over imagined trajectories. We introduce MA...
nodes.delta: [Manipulation • Action] Across diverse visual benchmarks including visual OGBench, MMBench2, Robomimic, and LIBERO-10, MAC-v2 achieves strong performance against model-free and model-based offline RL baselines.

nodes.title: KG-Neighbor: Knowledge-Guided Neighborhood Construction for Embedding Visualization
nodes.abstract: In embedding visualizations, nearby instances are interpreted as semantically related, although neighborhoods derived from input embeddings may not reflect content relationships. Neighborhood-based dimensionality reduction (DR) methods can propagate this limitation by optimizing layouts from embedding-based neighborhood graphs. We propose Knowledge-Guided Neighborhood Graph Construction (KGN), which represents relati...
nodes.delta: [Image • Visual] We also introduce IDProfile (IDP), which interprets residual mismatches by independently assessing whether the source content supports the assigned class label and the neighborhood-majority class.

nodes.title: Goal Revelation as a Bridge Between Information-Theoretic Empowerment and Capability-Based Human Power
nodes.abstract: Power matters for AI safety. Optimal agents tend to acquire power across a wide range of objectives (instrumental convergence). As we embed AI agents into socio-technical systems, humans risk gradual disempowerment. Both concerns call for a formal, quantitative measure of power. Two such measures in the context of Markov games are information-theoretic empowerment, the capacity of the channel from an agent's actions ...
nodes.delta: [Information • Risk] A satisfaction floor, computable from two statistics of interaction logs, offers a way to monitor the power users retain in a deployed system, and simulations in random environments show the three quantities are correlated but far from interchangeable.

nodes.title: TriAttention: Unified Sparse Mixed-Precision Attention for Long-Context LLM Inference
nodes.abstract: Sparsity and quantization reduce the cost of attention by skipping interactions and lowering the precision of those retained. However, useful interactions differ in their precision requirements: some tolerate low-precision scores while remaining sensitive to removal. We therefore introduce TriAttention, which assigns query-key (QK) tiles to skipping, 4-bit, or 8-bit computation, using 4-bit to retain quantization-tol...
nodes.delta: [Image • Visual] Experiments show that TriAttention achieves end-to-end generation speedups of up to 7.88x over the Torch attention and 2.65x over the BF16 baseline.

nodes.title: Evolutionary Adaptive Neighborhood Learning: A Genetic Algorithm for Instance-Dependent k Optimization in Nearest Neighbor Classification
nodes.abstract: The number of neighbours k is the central hyperparameter of the k-nearest neighbour (k-NN) classifier and is usually selected globally through cross-validation or evolutionary search. However, the bias-variance trade-off is inherently local: dense and noise-free regions may favour small neighbourhoods, whereas sparse or noisy regions may require larger ones. Since global-k optimization is one-dimensional, replacing e...
nodes.delta: [World • Forecasting] Under nested cross-validation, EANK achieves competitive performance relative to tuned global-k baselines and improves upon the default k=5.

nodes.title: How Deep is the Signal? Time-Context up to 30 Years for Colorectal Cancer Prediction in a Primary-Care EHR Model
nodes.abstract: EHR foundation models read medical events within a fixed context window, and long context has so far been measured only in tokens. How far back in time a model must look to capture the earliest predictive signal is unknown. We introduce time-context, the calendar lookback window before the prediction point, and provide, to our knowledge, the first systematic evaluation of decade-scale time-context for an EHR foundati...
nodes.delta: [Clinical • Medical] We introduce time-context, the calendar lookback window before the prediction point, and provide, to our knowledge, the first systematic evaluation of decade-scale time-context for an EHR foundation model.

nodes.title: Satisficing as competitive Bayesian weighting: a minimal model of goal-directed choice under an unattained target
nodes.abstract: Animals and humans often do not maximize; they act relative to goals (aspiration levels) that are frequently not yet met. How can a goal that is not (yet) realized organize choice? Deacon (2012) calls such absence-referenced organization \emph{ententional}, and García-Valdecasas and Deacon (2024) argue that ends are best understood as constraints rather than as particular states. We examine this idea in a minimal for...
nodes.delta: [Evolution • Self] ACB offers an analyzable model in which an unattained goal and a limited attentional resource jointly constrain behavior, and it yields testable predictions about how organisms revalue options they have abandoned.

nodes.title: Efficient Diffusion Policy Fine Tuning with Latent Noise Representation Bridging
nodes.abstract: Pre-trained diffusion and flow policies have emerged as powerful backbones for robotics, yet adapting them to novel data via reinforcement learning (RL) remains computationally expensive, sample inefficient and lacks theoretical guarantees. Prior approaches that fine-tune the initial noise bypass costly backpropagation through time but struggle with the "noise aliasing" problem: there does not exista natural link bet...
nodes.delta: [Manipulation • Action] Leveraging these insights, we propose Latent Representation Bridging for Diffusion (LARBRID), an algorithm that efficiently learns the representation to optimize the initial distribution that steers the pre-trained model to act optimally in the environment.

nodes.title: Encoding and Propagation of Grammatical Number in Large Language Models
nodes.abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) have become an increasingly popular means of translating Large Language Model (LLM) hidden state vectors into a human-comprehensible list of features or symbols. As such, SAEs may provide insight into an LLM's knowledge representation and internal ``mental'' grammar - topics of pragmatic interest for mechanistic interpretation of AI behavior and of theoretical interest for the study of in s...
nodes.delta: [Knowledge • Text] This asymmetry suggests that Pythia-70m makes use of a privative representation of grammatical number in English.

nodes.title: How Should Agents See Code? Rethinking Code Representations for Agentic Software Engineering
nodes.abstract: LLM agents are increasingly used for repository-level software engineering tasks. However, most agents still access repositories through raw files, lexical search, and shell commands, treating code primarily as text. This paper investigates map-based code-representation workflows as a design variable in agentic software engineering, examining how different repository views change agents' retrieval behavior, task succ...
nodes.delta: [Code • Skill] The results show that representation workflows are most useful as token-saving tools when localization is the bottleneck, while their success gains narrow when the decisive step is patch or test authoring.

nodes.title: Robust Ranking of Port Impacts from Impending Tropical Cyclones: A Two-Stage Recommendation System
nodes.abstract: When a tropical cyclone (TC) threatens several ports, preparedness planning depends on anticipating which ports are likely to be affected and where disruptions may last longest. Limited historical observations at individual ports and uncertainty in landfall location make these relative impacts difficult to estimate. We use a two-stage recommendation framework that first selects candidate ports based on their proximit...
nodes.delta: [World • Forecasting] Among the ranking models, Wide & Deep Learning achieves the closest agreement with the observed port rankings.

nodes.title: Permanent and Transient Representations for Continual Reinforcement Learning
nodes.abstract: Continual Reinforcement Learning (CRL) agents struggle to adapt to new situations while retaining prior knowledge, leading to a stability-plasticity trade-off. One approach to solving this problem is by using complementary learning systems: one for slow, long-term learning and another for quick, transient adaptation. Anand & Precup (2023) instantiated this idea using permanent and transient value functions, but used ...
nodes.delta: [Reinforcement • Reward] By introducing a novel non-parametric approximation for estimating the transient value function in complex tasks, we demonstrate that our method enables online learning and outperforms competitive baselines on image-based tasks and Craftax-Classic, underscoring the effectiveness of our system-level decomposition.

nodes.title: Selective Retrieval Routing for Multi-Violation Knowledge Graph Repair
nodes.abstract: Knowledge graphs often contain missing or inconsistent facts that undermine the applications built on them. Schema validation detects such violations but does not identify which of several valid repairs recovers the intended graph. External corpora can supply the evidence needed to identify the intended repair, but retrieving from them is costly and not always successful. We propose a framework for selective retrieva...
nodes.delta: [Information • Risk] It achieves higher repair [MATH] than always disabling access in five of six suites.

nodes.title: Test-Time Self-Play: Scaling without a Verifier
nodes.abstract: Test-time scaling methods spend additional compute at deployment to improve a large language model's performance on a hard target problem. Most methods rely on a verifier that scores candidate solutions for correctness, using it to select among or refine the model's outputs. In many deployment regimes, however, a strong verifier on the target problem is unavailable. We introduce Test-Time Self-Play (TTSP), an approac...
nodes.delta: [Manipulation • Action] We introduce Test-Time Self-Play (TTSP), an approach to test-time scaling using asymmetric self-play without reliance on a verifier.

nodes.title: EnvOpt: Automated Optimization for Agent Environments
nodes.abstract: An LLM agent's cost and success depend on its model, its harness, and its environment. In addition to the widely studied directions of parameter tuning and harness optimization, we propose the third direction: optimization over stationary environments. Agents are often deployed in rich environments shared by many tasks, such as a company's Slack workspace or a complex collection of data sources, documents or tickets....
nodes.delta: [Evolution • Self] More broadly, our results show that how information is represented to an agent shapes both its cost and its success, making the environment worth optimizing in addition to the parameters and the harness.

nodes.title: WeLM-Image: A Unified Image Generation Model towards Visual Intelligence
nodes.abstract: We present \textbf{WeLM-Image}, a unified image foundation model that integrates multimodal understanding into text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing, and multi-reference synthesis. Designed for single-GPU deployment in WeChat's large-scale consumer applications, the model processes text, reference images, and target latents as one interleaved sequence. A Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) backbone combines ...
nodes.delta: [Image • Visual] We present \textbf{WeLM-Image}, a unified image foundation model that integrates multimodal understanding into text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing, and multi-reference synthesis.

nodes.title: FreePath: Neural Mean Free Path for Image Dehazing
nodes.abstract: Single image dehazing requires recovering scene radiance from visual responses that are weakened and veiled by participating media. Existing methods either invert explicit scattering variables, which can be unstable under complex scenes, or learn direct restoration mappings, which often discard the physical organization of haze formation. We present \emph{FreePath}, a neural mean free path framework for image dehazin...
nodes.delta: [Image • Visual] Experiments on paired CDD-11 haze images and real RTTS scenes show that FreePath consistently improves full reference fidelity, no reference perceptual quality, and visual faithfulness over representative dehazing baselines.

nodes.title: PSGAgent: Enhancing MLLMs' Dynamic Visual Perception for Panoptic Scene Graph Generation via Agentic Reasoning
nodes.abstract: Panoptic Scene Graph generation (PSG) requires holistic yet fine-grained reasoning over complex relations among objects. However, current Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) applied to PSG suffer from a perception bottleneck: they function as static observers limited by fixed-resolution views. As a result, models often overlook critical relations involving small or peripheral objects and struggle to differentiat...
nodes.delta: [World • Forecasting] Extensive experiments on the PSG benchmark show that PSGAgent achieves SOTA performance, demonstrating strong capability in both holistic and fine-grained scene understanding.

nodes.title: Typed Knowledge over Constructive Institutions
nodes.abstract: Type theories designed for mathematics or program verification need only that a proposition holds; proof irrelevance in conversion erases, at the kernel level, how a claim was established. A persistent knowledge store, by contrast, must retain that record: who established a claim, by which derivation or external tool, and under which assumptions. This volume presents the theory of Eigenius---a store of typed knowledg...
nodes.delta: [Code • Skill] This volume presents the theory of Eigenius---a store of typed knowledge over constructive institutions---and develops its metatheory from that requirement.

nodes.title: IMUDINO: Self-distilled Foundation Model for Inertial Sensing
nodes.abstract: We present IMUDINO, the first foundation model (FM) for inertial sensing to achieve competitive performance across diverse sensing tasks including human activity recognition (HAR), health, motion capture, and odometry. Prior inertial FMs often focus on one subfield of inertial sensing and sometimes underperform state-of-the-art supervised methods (e.g., in HAR), making their scope considerably narrower than FMs for v...
nodes.delta: [World • Forecasting] We present IMUDINO, the first foundation model (FM) for inertial sensing to achieve competitive performance across diverse sensing tasks including human activity recognition (HAR), health, motion capture, and odometry.

nodes.title: The Last Mile to the Real World: Agent-Native Primitives as Reusable Building Blocks for Solving Real-World Tasks
nodes.abstract: How can an agent handle a real-world task end to end? Frontier models with their own harnesses still fall short on real-world benchmarks: on Terminal-Bench 4.0, GPT-5.6 Sol with Codex resolves 37.3% of the tasks and Claude Opus 5 with Claude Code 51.8%. These tasks fail at the step from reaching a resource to applying it, which we call the last mile to the real world. Existing approaches put the resource within reach...
nodes.delta: [Code • Skill] We introduce agent-native primitives, reusable units that equip a resource with a resident LLM that applies it in context and communicates with other primitives, and HEELO (Harness Engineering around Evolving Agent-Native Primitives for the Last Mile to Real-WOrld Tasks), a harness engineering framework that builds each task's harness from a library of such primitives.

nodes.title: FINCOSMOS: An Open-World Evaluation Paradigm for Agents in Finance
nodes.abstract: Language agents increasingly work for users on the open Web, and finance is where trusting them is hardest. The data must come from the Web, the strategy lives in the user's head, and correctness depends on time, so an agent can fail silently: a strategy the user never asked for, unverified data, or a backtest that uses the future yields a report as convincing as a correct one. Existing benchmarks close the world som...
nodes.delta: [Information • Risk] We introduce FINCOSMOS, an open-world evaluation paradigm for agents doing financial work.

nodes.title: Echoes of Error: Residual-Directional Local Rollout Consistency for Timeseries Forecasting
nodes.abstract: In time-series forecasting, rollout errors are not merely one-step fitting discrepancies: once fed back into the evolving state, they can perturb future predictions. We formalize this effect through local rollout consistency, which compares the next prediction produced under teacher forcing with that produced under free running. In principle, this consistency can be enforced directly by tracking the residual-induced ...
nodes.delta: [World • Forecasting] Experiments on time series forecasting tasks support this view, showing that the proposed regularization improves predictive accuracy.

nodes.title: Adversarial Robustness of Kernel Machines: A Comprehensive Analysis
nodes.abstract: Kernel machines are an important class of models in machine learning. However, the question of how robust modern kernel machines are to adversarial examples has not been studied comprehensively. In this paper, we provide a thorough empirical investigation of the adversarial robustness of kernel-based models for both binary and multiclass classification tasks, via white-box and black-box evasion attacks. We evaluate t...
nodes.delta: [Clinical • Medical] Our experiments on classification tasks on image and tabular datasets strongly indicate that kernel machines are natively more robust than neural networks, i.e., their performance degrades more gracefully against adversarial perturbations.

nodes.title: KOSMOS: Self-scheduling Persistent Kernels for Communication-Compute Overlap
nodes.abstract: Tensor and sequence parallelism (TP+SP) and expert parallelism (EP) put collectives on the critical path of transformer layers. State-of-the-art fused kernels mitigate this with fixed roles or schedules, but this rigidity leaves large idle windows. Predicting a communication-computation split does not remove them either; a predetermined split cannot follow data readiness. We present KOSMOS, a library for self-schedul...
nodes.delta: [World • Forecasting] We present KOSMOS, a library for self-scheduling persistent kernels whose workgroups use queues ordered by consumer demand to switch between communication and computation roles as data become ready, with no scheduler, per-call cost model, or tuned split.

nodes.title: Localization Does Not Imply Steerability: A Mechanistic Study of Sign Errors in LLM Mathematics
nodes.abstract: When large language models do multi-step mathematics, a characteristic failure recurs: the model writes one wrong sign token mid-computation -- a cofactor sign, the minus of a recursive integration-by-parts step -- then executes the rest of the arithmetic correctly, and the answer comes out wrong. We ask where inside the network that sign is written. Across six open models spanning 14B to 675B parameters, a per-layer...
nodes.delta: [Evolution • Self] The circuit is causal: subtracting a single sign direction from the residual stream flips 13 of 14 held-out minus-written integration-by-parts errors on Llama-3.3-70B, with flips replicating on Qwen, Gemma, and Mistral-Small (24-70% per cell), and with representation-level specificity -- the same dose breaks correctly-minus answers while sparing correct-plus answers where the direction is surgical (0/72 on Llama), and matched random-direction and control-layer interventions are null.

nodes.title: SAVeR$^2$: Reasoning-based Safety Alignment for Large Reasoning Models via Verifiable Rewards
nodes.abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) have achieved impressive performance via explicit Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning, yet this process introduces critical safety risks. We formalize LRM safety objectives as requiring non-malicious reasoning and answers, safety consistency, and explicit intent identification. We argue that existing alignment methods suffer from poor adversarial generalization, a significant ``safety tax''...
nodes.delta: [Safety • Memory] Extensive experiments on models ranging from 1.5B to 671B demonstrate that SAVeR[MATH] achieves superior safety performance and significantly lower over-refusal rates across multiple benchmarks without compromising general reasoning capabilities.

nodes.title: Signed but Not Safe: Requirement Integrity in Multi-Agent LLM Handoffs
nodes.abstract: Enterprise AI agents increasingly split a user's request across subagents and merge their results, and each handoff can summarize away, alter or ignore a requirement. We report a preregistered study with synthetic, exactly scorable tasks comparing free-text, structured JSON and signed requirement-manifest handoffs: the orchestrator extracts each requirement as a verbatim quote plus a checkable predicate, code signs t...
nodes.delta: [Information • Risk] Signing protects requirements in transit, not at extraction; the extraction step is the trust boundary.

nodes.title: DelegateEval: Evaluating Platforms for Personal External Service Agents
nodes.abstract: AI agents that work for an individual over time may also help that individual serve external clients. We define a personal external service agent as an agent authorized and continuously managed by a specific individual to accept client requests, deliver work, and provide ongoing support using that person's knowledge, experience, professional methods, and service boundaries. Such agents could allow individuals to serv...
nodes.delta: [Information • Risk] We present the framework and an experimental design.

nodes.title: Concertina: Embodying Manipulation and Cognition in One Diffusion Vision-Language Model
nodes.abstract: Most vision-language-action (VLA) policies decouple manipulation from cognition by bolting an external action mechanism onto a vision-language model (VLM)--either quantizing actions into discrete tokens whose errors bear no stable correspondence to physical displacements, or delegating continuous trajectory generation to a separate action expert whose gradients compete with or are blocked from updating the VLM backbo...
nodes.delta: [Manipulation • Action] On standard benchmarks, Concertina achieves 98.15% average success on regular LIBERO, 85.9% on the 10,030-task LIBERO-Plus benchmark, and 4.142 average completed chain length on CALVIN ABC-D.

nodes.title: Graph learning-assisted logic-based Benders decomposition for distributionally robust in-station train rescheduling under disruptions
nodes.abstract: Uncertainty in resource reopening times complicates train holding and rerouting decisions when resource closures coincide with arrival delays and processing-time extensions. We develop a rolling-horizon distributionally robust model that updates predictions of the remaining closure duration as observations of disruption resolution become available. The model jointly optimizes train routes, sequences, and timings. It ...
nodes.delta: [Manipulation • Action] Information comparisons on six representative instances showed that using observations of disruption resolution reduced mean total completion delay by approximately 21.7\%.

nodes.title: Goal-Branching LaCAM: Temporary Goals as Search Branches in Dense Multi-Agent Pathfinding
nodes.abstract: LaCAM is a search-based solver for multi-agent pathfinding (MAPF) that runs a depth-first search over joint configurations, using PIBT to generate successors and lazily adding single-agent constraints to explore alternatives. Although LaCAM is complete, it can struggle on dense, corridor-heavy instances because extracting blocking agents from deadlocks requires coordinated moves of several agents, often away from the...
nodes.delta: [Reinforcement • Reward] This paper proposes Goal-Branching, where blocking agents are given temporary goals, each tried as an additional branch of LaCAM's search.

nodes.title: Adaptive Experimentation Can Hide Model Error:Detection Limits and Falsification Budget
nodes.abstract: An experiment can be informative about the parameters of a working model and uninformative about whether that model is wrong. Adaptive design can reinforce this mismatch by repeatedly selecting settings where an incorrect model fits. We bound the power of any valid adequacy test in terms of the experimenter's own sampling distribution, then distinguish information absent from the selected data from information lost b...
nodes.delta: [Information • Risk] These results support separating parameter learning, model checking and detector performance; they do not establish a universally superior design policy or prospective scientific discovery.

nodes.title: Action-Conditioned VLM Monitoring for Autonomous Vehicle Semantic Anomalies
nodes.abstract: We study action-conditioned monitoring of autonomous-vehicle behavior in semantically unusual driving scenes. The target is whether the executed ego action is appropriate for the scene: the same scene can admit both normal and anomalous behavior, so visual unusualness alone does not determine the monitoring label. A Vision-Language Model (VLM) first predicts the scene-required action from an outcome-hidden video wind...
nodes.delta: [World • Forecasting] On 235 clips from 15 scenario families, the two-stage protocol with a fixed T-2.5 s window obtains 83.0% accuracy and anomaly recall 0.773, versus 74.5% and 0.536 for a single-stage video-only baseline; specificity is 0.880 versus 0.928.

nodes.title: CST-Bench: Benchmarking Counterfactual Spatial Transition Reasoning with Causal Transition On-Policy Self-Distillation
nodes.abstract: Spatial reasoning is a fundamental capability of multimodal large language models (MLLMs), yet existing benchmarks mainly focus on static scene understanding. When objects are moved or swapped, models must infer not only spatial relations but also how interventions change the scene state. To address this problem, we introduce CST-Bench, a benchmark for counterfactual spatial reasoning. CST-Bench contains 7,082 exampl...
nodes.delta: [World • Forecasting] We further formulate counterfactual spatial reasoning as causal state-transition modeling and propose CT-OPSD, which uses CST-Bench annotations to guide a teacher model in learning counterfactual state transitions and causal reasoning chains.

nodes.title: FlashOffloading: Low-Latency KV Cache Offloading for Long-Context LLM Serving
nodes.abstract: In large language model (LLM) serving systems, the key-value (KV) cache grows linearly with sequence length and concurrency, so long-context inference easily hits the high-bandwidth memory (HBM) capacity wall and results in low concurrency. Offloading the KV cache to host dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) frees HBM space and raises concurrency, but the additional cache management and host-to-device (H2D) load overh...
nodes.delta: [World • Forecasting] We present FlashOffloading, a host-DRAM-centric inference architecture that fully offloads the KV cache in both the prefill and decode phases.

nodes.title: The Memory Trap: Language Agents Overgeneralize from Benign Interactions
nodes.abstract: Language agents increasingly use persistent memory to record user preferences and procedures across sessions. We show that memory from benign interactions can cause unsafe or unreliable behavior on later tasks. We call this failure the memory trap. To study this issue, we compare behavior in sessions with and without memory across six frontier models (including Claude Sonnet, Opus, and Fable models and GPT-5.6). We e...
nodes.delta: [Safety • Memory] These findings demonstrate that even benign interactions can lead to serious risks from memory systems, and thus motivate the need for new research into ensuring that agents preserve the scope of their memories.

nodes.title: SKIM: Pruning Large Language Model Agents via Selective Knowledge Informed Masking
nodes.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed under structured generation, where grammar constraints enforce output format at inference time. Whereas existing compression methods target unconstrained generation, we first identify a fundamental mismatch: under structured generation, grammar constraints reduce the model's output distribution to valid tokens, and the logits matter most at the small set of ...
nodes.delta: [Judge • Recommender] Motivated by this finding, we propose SKIM (Selective Knowledge-Informed Masking), the first pruning and distillation framework for LLM agents under structured generation, with both stages guided by token role.

nodes.title: Stress Testing Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Against Covert Misalignment
nodes.abstract: As LLM agents advance rapidly in autonomy, the risk of hidden objectives that bypass safety constraints becomes increasingly plausible. Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring offers a key control mechanism by reading the agent's reasoning and flagging misalignment before it materializes into action, yet its reliability depends on the realism of the red-team it is stress-tested against. Existing red-teaming efforts rely on...
nodes.delta: [Information • Risk] To counter these vulnerabilities, we propose a Bayesian Trajectory Monitoring framework, integrating global context and local segment evidence to detect covert misalignment.

nodes.title: Learning and Steering in Incomplete-Information Games
nodes.abstract: In many modern multi-agent systems, a mediator seeks to influence strategic decision dynamics using only outcome-level feedback and without knowing agents' utilities. In this work, we study how a mediator can learn an unknown game and steer adaptive agents toward outcomes that maximize her utility using only trajectory feedback. The mediator knows the game form and her own objective, but not the agents' utilities. Mo...

nodes.title: Evolver: Turning Agent Exploration into Evolving Capabilities
nodes.abstract: Agent exploration produces valuable procedural knowledge, yet much of this experience remains confined to transient execution traces and is not systematically reused. We introduce Evolver, an experience-driven framework that transforms agent exploration into persistent, reusable capabilities without updating foundation model parameters. Built around structured Gene assets, Evolver integrates experience acquisition, r...
nodes.delta: [Evolution • Self] We introduce Evolver, an experience-driven framework that transforms agent exploration into persistent, reusable capabilities without updating foundation model parameters.

nodes.title: Align Before Aggregation: Basis-Consistent Federated LoRA under Heterogeneous Ranks
nodes.abstract: Federated fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) under heterogeneous client capacities is increasingly important, and low-rank adaptation (LoRA) with heterogeneous ranks makes it practical. Existing server-side aggregators compose local matrix updates [MATH] from client-specific LoRA factors [MATH] before aggregating them. nodes.title: FisherDistill: Diffusion Distribution Distillation via Closed-Form Fisher Critics
nodes.abstract: Recent advances in diffusion distillation have enabled high-quality image generation in only one or a few network function evaluations (NFEs). Despite their efficiency, aggressively distilled generators often retain a residual distribution gap from their multi-step teachers, motivating recent methods to introduce adversarial refinement with a learned discriminator. In this work, we ask whether such refinement necessa...
nodes.delta: [Image • Visual] Using intermediate representations from the frozen teacher, we estimate the first- and second-order statistics of real and generated samples and derive a closed-form Fisher direction that maximally separates their feature distributions relative to within-class variation.

nodes.title: Embedding-Space Fingerprinting of LoRA Fine-Tunes: Recovering the Training-Data Domain from the Model Artifact Alone
nodes.abstract: When a base language model is fine-tuned with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), how much of the training data domain leaks into the resulting artifact? This paper studies whether a simple classifier can recover the domain of a fine-tune given only the model artifact (weight deltas, internal activations on a fixed probe set, or generated text) without ever observing the training data. Using one base model (Qwen3.5-0.8B), 36...

nodes.title: The Popular Get More Popular: Auditing Brand Bias in Generative Search
nodes.abstract: The shift from traditional to generative search has fundamentally transformed online product discovery. Because conversational recommendations synthesize choices into a few direct answers, subtle systemic preferences toward specific providers can exert profound commercial impacts. In this work, we audit this phenomenon through two distinct dimensions: (i) brand popularity bias, the systematic preference for market-do...
nodes.delta: [Judge • Recommender] Taken together, our findings demonstrate that generative search engines reinforce a ``rich-get-richer'' dynamic by favoring established market leaders and imposing a parametric barrier to entry that standard content optimization cannot overcome.

nodes.title: Beneath the Surface: What We Overlook When We Talk About Agent Evolution
nodes.abstract: Agent harness evolution enables recursive self-improvement (RSI) without updating model weights. We examine whether higher benchmark scores yield reliable, efficient, and transferable improvement. We evaluate four methods across harnesses, general and coding tasks. nodes.delta: [Evolution • Self] Specific changes usually outperform generic reminders, but their benefits can change when combined.

nodes.title: Redacting Personal Data: A Speed and Accuracy Comparison of Regex, Presidio and Hybrid Designs
nodes.abstract: Many enterprise projects now pass free text to large language models (LLMs), and that text often contains personally identifiable information (PII) such as names, phone numbers, email addresses, home addresses and dates of birth. nodes.title: Measuring the Marginal Value of Verifier-Based RL Beyond Supervised Fine-Tuning
nodes.abstract: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR) is usually evaluated as an alternative to supervised fine-tuning (SFT), or as a stage that follows it, with the implicit assumption that the RL stage contributes gains of its own. nodes.abstract: Current autonomous logical systems rely on a fragile assumption: that language models should dynamically write code, guess API payloads, and memorize operational constraints through prompt engineering. nodes.abstract: Drug discovery requires continuous scientific decision-making across a vast research space. nodes.title: Energy-Aware Open-Vocabulary Detection Scheduling for Low-Power Robotic Autonomy
nodes.abstract: Open-vocabulary object detection (OVD) lets robots search for run-time object queries, but fixed-rate inference spends embedded compute on low-value frames during idle motion, map revisits, or stable viewpoints. nodes.title: Who Should Know What? Empirical Information Design for Multi-Agent LLM Economies
nodes.abstract: The performance of multi-agent LLM systems depends not only on the capabilities of the underlying models but also on information-sharing policies, which govern what information each agent observes and at what level of detail. nodes.title: ReferClaw: Disambiguating User Intent for Egocentric Assistance
nodes.abstract: Users of egocentric AI assistants often ask short, ambiguous questions whose intended referents cannot be uniquely resolved from video and dialogue history. nodes.title: MCPHallu: Benchmarking Reasoning, Execution, and Memory Hallucinations in MCP Agents
nodes.abstract: Large language model agents are increasingly deployed through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), which allows them to discover and invoke tools across multiple servers at runtime. nodes.title: InfMasking: A Unified Variational Framework for Synergistic Multimodal Learning
nodes.abstract: Multimodal models are expected to exploit synergistic information, that is, information available only when multiple modalities are observed together. nodes.abstract: Selecting a next motion in a populated scene is not just a matter of avoiding what is currently in the way: an action can be locally feasible yet drift onto the road instead of the crosswalk, cut into a stream of crossing pedestrians, or bottleneck a narrow passage. nodes.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to simulate human behavior, their operational validity is typically assessed through accuracy alone, implicitly treating human behavior as deterministic. nodes.title: The Intrusion Pathway: How Non-Evidential Context Degrades Language Model Performance
nodes.abstract: Language models lose accuracy when a prompt contains non-evidential context: irrelevant statements from unrelated domains, or random off-distribution tokens, with no competing answer and no semantic overlap with the query. nodes.abstract: Goal interpretation is to translate a natural language instruction into a formal symbolic goal that a planner can execute. nodes.abstract: Recommender systems are transitioning from static retrieval engines into interactive assistants grounded in physical environments. nodes.title: MambaLoc: Lightweight Indoor Localization Using Cross-Modal Knowledge Distillation
nodes.abstract: Accurate indoor localization on resource-constrained edge devices remains challenging due to the tension between modeling fidelity and computational efficiency. nodes.title: LSRP*: Scalable and Anytime Planning for Multi-Agent Path Finding with Asynchronous Actions
nodes.abstract: Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) seeks collision-free paths for multiple agents from their respective starting locations to their respective goal locations while minimizing path costs. nodes.title: CPNav: Calibrated Vision-Language Navigation for Object-Goal Search in Unseen Environments
nodes.abstract: Directing a robot to locate a target object in unseen environments remains a central challenge in embodied AI. nodes.title: FEROM: Frontier Endogenous Reveal-Order Marginal Policy Optimization for Masked Diffusion LMs

nodes.title: The Limits of Information-Flow Control Enforcement for Agentic Systems

nodes.title: Too Big to Inspect? Ethically Auditing Large Datasets Through Small Samples

nodes.title: What Broke & Why: Practical Lessons from Reinforcement Learning Post-Training
